+# Configure integration profiles for generated playbooks - Microsoft Defender XDR | Microsoft Learn
+
+Integration profiles define the API connection details used by generated playbooks. Configure integration profiles before you create or run generated playbooks that call Microsoft or third-party services.
+
+Each integration profile includes connection details such as the base API URL, authentication method, and required credentials.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+Before you begin, make sure that:
+
+- You have access to the [Microsoft Defender portal](https://security.microsoft.com/).
+- You have the **Automation Integration** Unified RBAC permission with **Read** and **Write** access.
+- You have the credentials required for the target API.
+- To run automation on third-party data ingested through Log Analytics, you have a [Microsoft Sentinel workspace](/en-us/azure/sentinel/quickstart-onboard).
+
+## Create an integration profile
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Defender portal](https://security.microsoft.com/).
+2. Go to **Microsoft Sentinel** > **Configuration** > **Automation**.
+3. Select the **Integration Profiles** tab.
+4. Select **Create**.
+5. Enter an integration name.
+6. Enter a description.
+7. Enter the base API URL for the service.
+8. Select the authentication method.
+
+    Supported authentication methods include:
+
+    - OAuth2 Client Credentials
+    - API Key
+    - AWS Auth
+    - User and Password
+    - Bearer/JWT Authentication
+    - Hawk
+9. Enter the required authentication details.
+10. Review the integration profile settings.
+11. Select **Create**.
+
+## Create a Microsoft Graph integration profile
+
+Use a Microsoft Graph integration profile when a generated playbook needs to call Microsoft Graph APIs.
+
+1. In the Azure portal, go to **Microsoft Entra ID** > **App registrations**.
+2. Select **New registration**.
+3. Enter a name for the application.
+4. Complete the app registration.
+5. Copy the **Application (client) ID** and **Directory (tenant) ID**.
+6. Go to **Certificates & secrets**.
+7. Select **New client secret**.
+8. Copy the client secret value and store it securely.
+
+    Important
+
+    You can't retrieve the client secret value after leaving the page.
+9. Sign in to the [Microsoft Defender portal](https://security.microsoft.com/).
+10. Go to **Microsoft Sentinel** > **Configuration** > **Automation**.
+11. Select the **Integration Profiles** tab.
+12. Select **Create**.
+13. Configure the profile with the following values:
+
+    | Field | Value |
+    | --- | --- |
+    | Integration name | Enter a descriptive name, such as `Graph Integration`. |
+    | Description | Enter a short description. |
+    | Base API URL | `https://graph.microsoft.com` |
+    | Authentication method | OAuth2 |
+    | Client ID | Enter the Application client ID. |
+    | Client secret | Enter the client secret value. |
+    | Token endpoint | `https://login.microsoftonline.com/{TENANT_ID}/oauth2/v2.0/token` |
+    | Scopes | `https://graph.microsoft.com/.default` |
+14. Replace `{TENANT_ID}` with the Directory tenant ID.
+15. Select **Create**.
+
+## Edit an integration profile
+
+You can edit the integration name and description after the profile is created.
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Defender portal](https://security.microsoft.com/).
+2. Go to **Microsoft Sentinel** > **Configuration** > **Automation**.
+3. Select the **Integration Profiles** tab.
+4. Select the integration profile.
+5. Update the name or description.
+6. Save your changes.
+
+Note
+
+The API URL and authentication method can't be changed after an integration profile is created. To change the API URL or authentication method, create a new integration profile.
+
+## Limitations
+
+Integration profiles have the following limitations:
+
+- Microsoft Graph and Azure Resource Manager integrations aren't enabled by default and must be manually created.
+- The API URL and authentication method can't be changed after an integration profile is created.
+- The maximum number of integrations per tenant is 500.

+# Manage tables, tiers, and retention in ISOC | Microsoft Learn
+
+Integrated Security Operations Center (ISOC) in Microsoft Defender supports Microsoft security data and additional Microsoft and non-Microsoft security data.
+
+## How data is handled
+
+Native Microsoft Defender data is available directly in the Microsoft Defender experience and doesn't need to be separately ingested into an ISOC workspace.
+
+Other supported Microsoft and non-Microsoft data can be connected through an ISOC workspace by using [data connectors](/en-us/azure/sentinel/connect-data-sources?tabs=defender-portal).
+
+## Microsoft security data
+
+ISOC supports Microsoft security data from the following sources:
+
+- Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
+- Microsoft Defender for Office 365
+- Microsoft Defender for Identity
+- Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps
+- Microsoft Defender for Cloud
+- Microsoft Entra
+- Azure Activity through a connector
+- Office 365 Activity through a connector
+
+Eligible customers with Microsoft Defender Suite, Microsoft 365 E5, or Microsoft 365 E7 can use supported Microsoft Defender security data as part of the ISOC experience.
+
+For Microsoft 365 E5 plan details and pricing, see [Microsoft 365 E5 for Enterprise](https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/enterprise/e5#Pricing).
+
+To compare the security capabilities included with Microsoft 365 enterprise plans, see [Microsoft 365 Security Enterprise Plans](https://www.microsoft.com/security/pricing/enterprise-plans).
+
+### 90-day retention
+
+Starting November 15, 2026, eligible customers receive up to 90 days of included retention for supported Microsoft Defender data, Azure Activity data, and Office 365 Activity data at no additional charge.
+
+The retention benefit applies at the workload level, except for the tables listed in Retention exceptions. As additional supported tables become available for an included workload, they're also included in the retention benefit unless otherwise noted.
+
+The following tables and data sources are currently included:
+
+- **Alerts**
+
+    - `AlertEvidence`
+    - `AlertInfo`
+- **Azure Activity**
+- **Behaviors**
+
+    - `BehaviorEntities`
+    - `BehaviorInfo`
+- **Microsoft Defender for Cloud**
+
+    - `BehaviorInfo`
+    - `BehaviorEntities`
+    - `CloudStorageEvents`
+    - `CloudStorageAggregatedEventsV2`
+    - `CloudPolicyEnforcementEvents`
+    - `CloudKeyVaultEvents`
+    - `CloudKeyVaultRawEvents`
+    - `CloudHttpIncomingEvents`
+    - `CloudProcessEvents`
+    - `CloudStorageAggregatedEvents`
+    - `CloudAuditEvents`
+    - `CloudDnsEvents`
+- **Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps**
+
+    - `CloudAppEvents`
+    - `OAuthAppInfo`
+- **Microsoft Defender for Endpoint**
+
+    - `DeviceEvents`
+    - `DeviceFileCertificateInfo`
+    - `DeviceFileEvents`
+    - `DeviceImageLoadEvents`
+    - `DeviceInfo`
+    - `DeviceLogonEvents`
+    - `DeviceNetworkEvents`
+    - `DeviceNetworkInfo`
+    - `DeviceProcessEvents`
+    - `DeviceRegistryEvents`
+    - `DisruptionAndResponseEvents`
+- **Microsoft Defender for Identity**
+
+    - `IdentityDirectoryEvents`
+    - `IdentityEvents`
+    - `IdentityLogonEvents`
+    - `IdentityQueryEvents`
+- **Microsoft Defender for Office 365**
+
+    - `CallActivityEvents`
+    - `CampaignInfo`
+    - `EmailAttachmentInfo`
+    - `EmailEvents`
+    - `EmailPostDeliveryEvents`
+    - `EmailUrlInfo`
+    - `FileMaliciousContentInfo`
+    - `MessageEvents`
+    - `MessagePostDeliveryEvents`
+    - `MessageUrlInfo`
+    - `UrlClickEvents`
+- **Microsoft Entra**
+
+    - `EntraIdDirectoryAuditEvents`
+    - `EntraIdSignInEvents`
+    - `EntraIdSpnSignInEvents`
+    - `GraphAPIAuditEvents`
+- **Office 365 Activity**
+
+### Extend Microsoft Defender data retention
+
+When you enable streaming for supported Microsoft Defender data, the retention period starts at 180 days.
+
+Extended retention applies to new data after you enable it. Data that was collected before you enabled extended retention isn't backfilled.
+
+Additional charges apply when you extend retention beyond the retention included with ISOC.
+
+### Retention exceptions
+
+The following tables don't receive the 90-day included retention benefit. They're stored in XDR for 30 days. As with other supported tables, extended retention starts at 180 days.
+
+| Table | Retention in XDR | Extended retention starts at |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `AgentsInfo` | 30 days. | 180 days. |
+| `IdentityAccountInfo` | 30 days. | 180 days. |
+
+## Additional Microsoft and non-Microsoft security data
+
+An ISOC workspace is required to ingest additional Microsoft and non-Microsoft security data through [more than 500 data connectors](/en-us/azure/sentinel/data-connectors-reference).
+
+Additional Microsoft and non-Microsoft security data is billed separately from the Microsoft security data included with the ISOC benefit. Ingested data can be retained for up to 90 days as part of the ISOC ingestion experience.
+
+Additional ingestion and retention charges might apply depending on the data you ingest and how long you retain it.
+
+## How data tiers and retention work
+
+You can retain data in one of two tiers:
+
+- **Analytics tier**: This tier makes data available for alerting, hunting, workbooks, and more. It retains data in two states:
+
+    - **Analytics retention**: In this "hot" state, data is fully available for real-time analytics, including high-performance queries, analytics rules, and threat hunting. By default, supported Microsoft Defender XDR tables retain data in this tier for 90 days, except for the tables listed in Retention exceptions. You can extend the retention period of supported tables at a prorated monthly long-term retention charge.
+    - **Total retention**: By default, all data in the analytics tier is mirrored to the data lake for the same retention period. You can extend the retention of your data in the lake beyond the analytics retention, for up to 12 years of total retention at a low cost.
+- **Data Lake tier**: In this low-cost "cold" tier, ISOC retains your data in the data lake only. Data in the Data Lake tier isn't available for real-time analytics features and threat hunting. However, you can access data in the lake whenever you need it through [KQL jobs](datalake/kql-jobs), analyze trends over time by running scheduled KQL or Spark jobs, and aggregate insights from incoming data at a regular cadence by using summary rules.
+- **XDR data**: Except for the tables listed in Retention exceptions, supported Microsoft Defender XDR threat hunting data is available in the Analytics tier for 90 days by default. Extending retention beyond 90 days in the Analytics tier incurs ingestion and storage costs. You can also ingest exclusively into the Data Lake tier, but supported data remains available in the Analytics tier for its included retention period. Ingesting XDR data directly into the Data Lake tier is more cost-effective, but it involves ingestion, storage, and processing costs.
+
+For more information about the differences between the Analytics tier and the Data Lake tier, see Compare the analytics and data lake tiers.
+
+For more information about the Microsoft Sentinel data lake, see [What is Microsoft Sentinel data lake](datalake/sentinel-lake-overview).
+
+## Compare the analytics and data lake tiers
+
+This table compares the Analytics and Data Lake tiers and their key characteristics:
+
+| Comparison | Analytics tier | Data Lake tier |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Key characteristics | High-performance querying and indexing for logs (also known as hot, or interactive retention). | Cost-effective long-term retention of large data volumes (also known as cold storage). |
+| Best for | Real-time analytics rules, alerting, hunting, workbooks, and all Microsoft Sentinel features. | - Compliance and regulatory logging.- Historical trend analysis and forensics.- Low-touch data that's not needed for real-time alerts. |
+| Ingestion cost | Standard | Minimal |
+| Query price included | ✅ | ❌ |
+| Optimized query performance | ✅ | ❌ Slower queries.Good for auditing. Not optimized for real-time analysis. |
+| Query capabilities | [Full query capabilities](/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/get-started-queries) in the Microsoft Defender portal, the Azure portal, and by using APIs. | - [Full query capabilities](/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/get-started-queries), including unions and joins.- Run scheduled KQL or Spark jobs.- Use notebooks. |
+| Full set of real-time analytics features | ✅ | ❌ Limitations on some features, including analytics rules, hunting queries, parsers, watchlists, workbooks, and playbooks. |
+| [Search jobs](investigate-large-datasets) | ✅ | ✅ |
+| [Summary rules](summary-rules) | ✅ | ✅ [Full KQL on a single table](/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/basic-logs-query), which you can extend with data from an analytics table using [lookup](/en-us/azure/data-explorer/kusto/query/lookup-operator) |
+| [Restore](restore) | ✅ | ❌ KQL and Notebook jobs can promote data to the analytics tier. |
+| [Data export](/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/logs-data-export) | ✅ | ❌ |
+| Retention period | 90 days for Microsoft Sentinel and supported Microsoft Defender XDR tables, subject to Retention exceptions.You can extend retention for supported tables at a prorated monthly long-term retention charge. | Same as analytics retention, by default. Can be extended to up to 12 years. |
+
+## What happens when you modify table settings
+
+You can switch a table's tier and retention settings at any time.
+
+When you change a table's tier from Analytics to Data Lake, all real-time analytics and hunting queries stop working.
+
+When you shorten a table's total retention, Microsoft waits 30 days before removing the data, so you can revert the change and avoid data loss if you made a configuration error.
+
+When you increase total retention, the new retention period applies to all data that was already ingested into the table and wasn't yet removed.
+
+When you change the analytics retention settings of a table with existing data, the change takes effect immediately.
+
+***Example***:
+
+- You have a table in the Analytics tier with 180 days of analytics retention. By default, total retention is also set to 180 days.
+- You change analytics retention to 90 days without changing total retention, which remains 180 days.
+- ISOC automatically removes the last 90 days of data from analytics retention, but continues to store data that's 90-180 days old in the Data Lake tier.
+
+## Manage table settings
+
+To configure table retention and tier settings in the Microsoft Defender portal, follow these steps:
+
+1. Select **Setup & Configuration** > **Data management** > **Data & connectors** from the left navigation pane.
+
+    The **Tables** page lists all the tables you can manage in the Microsoft Defender portal and each table's current settings.
+2. Select a table on the **Tables** screen.
+
+    Selecting a table opens the table details side panel with more information about the table, including data sources, table description, tier, and retention details.
+
+    [![Screenshot that shows the table details side panel for the CommonSecurityLog table, including data sources, on the Table Management screen in the Defender portal.](media/manage-data-overview/table-management-microsoft-defender-portal.png)](media/manage-data-overview/table-management-microsoft-defender-portal.png#lightbox)
+3. Select **Manage table**.
+
+    The **Manage table** screen lets you modify retention settings in the current tier and change the storage tier, if necessary.
+
+    Available settings depend on the table. Review the options and warnings shown for the selected table rather than assuming that every table supports the full ranges listed here.
+
+    [![Screenshot that shows the Manage table screen for the CommonSecurityLog table in the Defender portal.](media/manage-data-overview/manage-table-settings-microsoft-defender-portal.png)](media/manage-data-overview/manage-table-settings-microsoft-defender-portal.png#lightbox)
+
+    - **Analytics tier retention settings**:
+
+        - **Analytics retention**: Select a retention period from the available values for the table.
+        - **Total retention**: Set a value up to 12 years of long-term storage in the Data Lake.
+    - **Data Lake tier**: Set **Retention** to a value between 30 days and 12 years. Selecting **Data Lake tier** stores data exclusively in the Data Lake.
+    - **Tier changes**: If necessary, you can change tiers at any time based on your cost management and data usage needs.
+
+        Important
+
+        Tier changes aren't available for all tables. For example, some tables must remain in the Analytics tier because Microsoft security services require the data in these tables for near-real-time analytics.
+
+    For more information about retention and tier settings, see How data tiers and retention work.
+4. Review warnings and messages. These messages help you understand important implications of changing table settings.
+
+    Examples include:
+
+    - Increased retention is likely to increase data cost.
+    - Changing from the Analytics tier to the Data Lake tier causes features that rely on Analytics data to stop functioning, such as:
+        - Alerting
+        - Advanced hunting
+        - Analytics rules
+        - Custom detection rules
+5. Select **Save** to apply the new settings.
+
+## Retention pricing
+
+When you change a table's retention settings in **Manage table**, you might see an estimated retention price. This price shows the cost of retaining 1 GB of ingested data for the full selected retention period.
+
+The estimate includes the components described below, not your total data cost.
+
+The components depend on the tier you ingest data into and the type of data, as described in the following sections. The examples use illustrative rates in US dollars (USD).
+
+Data Lake storage is charged per GB per month, based on a uniform data compression rate of 6:1. For example, 600 GB of raw data is billed as 100 GB of compressed data. For each 1 GB of ingested data, storage charges therefore apply to 1/6 GB.
+
+### Analytics tier
+
+The estimate can include two components:
+
+- **Extended analytics retention**: A charge for extending analytics retention, based on the type of data.
+- **Data Lake storage**: A charge for keeping data in the data lake after its analytics retention period ends.
+
+For example, 180 days of analytics retention and 270 days of total retention adds 90 days, or three months, of Data Lake storage charges. There's no separate Data Lake ingestion or processing charge.
+
+#### Microsoft Defender XDR data
+
+For supported Microsoft Defender XDR tables with 90 days of included retention, the minimum extended analytics retention period is 180 days. A per-GB charge covers the first 180 days. Analytics retention beyond 180 days is charged per GB per month.
+
+**Example:** You retain data for 180 days in the Analytics tier and 270 days in total.
+
+Assume an analytics retention charge of $1.20 per GB and a Data Lake storage rate of $0.026 per GB per month.
+
+- Analytics retention for the first 180 days: $1.20 per GB.
+- Data Lake storage for the remaining 90 days: 3 × 1/6 × $0.026 = $0.013 per GB.
+
+The estimated retention price is $1.20 + $0.013 = **$1.213 per GB**.
+
+**Example:** You retain data for 270 days in the Analytics tier, with the same total retention period.
+
+Assume a charge of $1.20 per GB for the first 180 days and an analytics retention rate of $0.10 per GB per month beyond 180 days.
+
+The additional 90 days cost 3 × $0.10 = $0.30 per GB. The estimated retention price is $1.20 + $0.30 = **$1.50 per GB**. There's no additional Data Lake storage charge because total retention equals analytics retention.
+
+#### Additional Microsoft and non-Microsoft security data
+
+Analytics retention beyond the included 90 days is charged per GB per month. The estimate shows the added retention cost. Existing Analytics tier ingestion charges are separate and aren't included.
+
+**Example:** You retain data for 180 days in the Analytics tier and 270 days in total.
+
+Assume an analytics retention rate of $0.10 per GB per month and a Data Lake storage rate of $0.026 per GB per month.
+
+- Analytics retention beyond the included 90 days: 3 × $0.10 = $0.30 per GB.
+- Data Lake storage for the remaining 90 days: 3 × 1/6 × $0.026 = $0.013 per GB.
+
+The estimated added retention price is $0.30 + $0.013 = **$0.313 per GB**.
+
+### Data Lake tier
+
+When you ingest Microsoft Defender XDR data or additional Microsoft and non-Microsoft security data directly into the Data Lake tier, the estimate combines three components:
+
+- **Ingestion**: A per-GB charge for ingesting the data.
+- **Processing**: A per-GB charge for processing the ingested data.
+- **Data Lake storage**: A charge per GB per month for the selected retention period.
+
+**Example:** You ingest data directly into the Data Lake tier and retain it for 180 days, or six months.
+
+Assume rates of $0.05 per GB for ingestion, $0.10 per GB for processing, and $0.026 per GB per month for storage.
+
+- Ingestion: $0.05 per GB.
+- Processing: $0.10 per GB.
+- Data Lake storage for six months: 6 × 1/6 × $0.026 = $0.026 per GB.
+
+The estimated retention price is $0.05 + $0.10 + $0.026 = **$0.176 per GB**.

+# Update Microsoft Sentinel content to use Advanced Hunting tables | Microsoft Learn
+
+When you transition Microsoft Sentinel content from workspace-based Microsoft Defender data to Microsoft Defender XDR Advanced Hunting data, review the queries and dependent content that use the affected tables.
+
+Most Microsoft Defender tables have the same name in Microsoft Sentinel and Advanced Hunting, so table references usually don't change. However, some columns and data types work differently and require updates.
+
+Important
+
+Before you stop ingestion, update and validate all dependent queries, detections, workbooks, and automation for all Defender XDR tables. **Configure workspace** stops ingestion for the supported Defender XDR tables at the same time. If ingestion stops first, dependent content might reference data that is no longer arriving in the Microsoft Sentinel workspace.
+
+For the full Advanced Hunting schema, see [Understand the Advanced Hunting schema](/en-us/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-schema-tables).
+
+## Summary of required updates by workload
+
+The following sections group the affected tables by Microsoft Defender workload. Use the **Update pattern** column to identify the changes that apply to your content.
+
+### Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
+
+| Updates required | Tables | Update pattern |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| More content updates | `DeviceInfo` | Pattern 1 and Other column changes |
+| More content updates | `DeviceNetworkInfo` | Pattern 2 |
+| Some content updates | `DeviceEvents`, `DeviceFileEvents`, `DeviceProcessEvents`, `DeviceLogonEvents`, `DeviceNetworkEvents` | Pattern 1 |
+| Minor content updates | `DeviceFileCertificateInfo`, `DeviceImageLoadEvents`, `DeviceRegistryEvents` | Changes that apply to all tables |
+| More content updates | [`DisruptionAndResponseEvents`](/en-us/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-disruptionandresponseevents-table) | Other column changes |
+
+The `MachineGroup` column isn't consistently available or populated across Microsoft Defender XDR endpoint tables. Don't rely on `MachineGroup` for filtering or scoping outside `DeviceInfo`. If your queries, workbooks, analytics rules, or automation use this column, review and validate those implementations in Advanced Hunting before you stop ingestion.
+
+### Microsoft Defender for Office 365
+
+| Updates required | Tables | Update pattern |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| More content updates | `EmailEvents` | Pattern 1 and Other column changes |
+| Minor content updates | `EmailAttachmentInfo`, `EmailUrlInfo`, `UrlClickEvents` | Changes that apply to all tables |
+| More content updates | `EmailPostDeliveryEvents` | Other column changes |
+| More content updates | `MessageEvents`, `MessagePostDeliveryEvents`, `MessageUrlInfo` | Microsoft Teams message tables |
+| More content updates | [`CallActivityEvents`](/en-us/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-callactivityevents-table), [`FileMaliciousContentInfo`](/en-us/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-filemaliciouscontentinfo-table) | Other column changes |
+| Minor content updates | [`CampaignInfo`](/en-us/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-campaigninfo-table) | Changes that apply to all tables |
+
+#### Microsoft Teams message tables
+
+In addition to the changes that apply to all tables, check these column differences:
+
+| Table | Microsoft Sentinel | Advanced Hunting | What to do |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| `MessageEvents` | `MessageSubject`, `MessageFormatType`, `MessageFormatSubtype` | Not available | Remove these columns. Use `Subject` for the message subject. |
+| `MessageEvents` | `LastEditedTime` (string) | `LastEditedTime` (datetime) | For text comparisons, use `tostring(LastEditedTime)`. |
+| `MessagePostDeliveryEvents` | `DetectionMethods` (string) | `DetectionMethods` (dynamic) | For text comparisons, use `tostring(DetectionMethods)`. |
+| `MessageUrlInfo` | `ThreatTypes` | Not available | Join with `MessageEvents` on `TeamsMessageId` to get the threat verdict. |
+| `MessageUrlInfo` | Not available | `UrlLocation` | You can use this new column. |
+
+This table reflects the schema that Advanced Hunting returns. Columns not listed work the same in both. If a column differs from the schema reference page, run `<TableName> | getschema` in Advanced Hunting to confirm.
+
+For the full schemas, see [MessageEvents](/en-us/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-messageevents-table), [MessagePostDeliveryEvents](/en-us/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-messagepostdeliveryevents-table), and [MessageUrlInfo](/en-us/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-messageurlinfo-table).
+
+### Microsoft Defender for Identity
+
+| Updates required | Tables | Update pattern |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| More content updates | `IdentityLogonEvents`, `IdentityDirectoryEvents`, `IdentityQueryEvents` | Pattern 3 |
+| Minor content updates | [`IdentityEvents`](/en-us/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-identityevents-table) | Changes that apply to all tables |
+
+### Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps and Defender alerts
+
+| Updates required | Tables | Update pattern |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| More content updates | `AlertEvidence` | Pattern 1, Pattern 4, and Other column changes |
+| Minor content updates | `CloudAppEvents`, `AlertInfo` | Changes that apply to all tables |
+| Minor content updates | [`OAuthAppInfo`](/en-us/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-oauthappinfo-table) | Changes that apply to all tables |
+
+### Microsoft Defender for Cloud
+
+| Updates required | Tables | Update pattern |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| More content updates | [`CloudAuditEvents`](/en-us/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-cloudauditevents-table), [`CloudDnsEvents`](/en-us/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-clouddnsevents-table), [`CloudProcessEvents`](/en-us/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-cloudprocessevents-table) | Other column changes |
+
+Note
+
+Defender is still building up 90 days of history for Defender for Cloud tables. Until it does, Advanced Hunting might have less than 90 days of past data for these tables. If you need older data, keep it in Microsoft Sentinel until Advanced Hunting has the history you need.
+
+## Changes that apply to all tables
+
+Review the following changes for every query, detection, workbook, and playbook that you update:
+
+- You don't have to replace `TimeGenerated`. When your Microsoft Sentinel workspace is connected to the Microsoft Defender portal, `TimeGenerated` in Advanced Hunting returns the same value as the table's event time column. In Microsoft Sentinel, `TimeGenerated` can differ slightly from the event time, so results that depend on exact time windows might not match exactly. For new queries, and for custom detections that run in near real time (**Continuous (NRT)** frequency), use `Timestamp`. `CallActivityEvents` doesn't have a `Timestamp` column. For that table, use `ActivityTimestamp`.
+- Remove dependencies on Sentinel-only metadata columns such as `TenantId`, `SourceSystem`, `_IsBillable`, and `_BilledSize`.
+- For device tables, review dependencies on `MachineGroup`. Don't rely on `MachineGroup` for filtering or scoping outside `DeviceInfo`.
+- Update playbooks that query Log Analytics to use the Advanced Hunting API. For more information, see [Update Logic App playbook automation](transition-logic-app-playbooks).
+- Validate Microsoft Defender permissions and scoping for analysts, workbook viewers, and automation identities. For more information, see [Update permissions and roles with Unified RBAC](transition-unified-rbac).
+- Advanced Hunting tables don't include custom columns that end in `_CF`. These columns are added by a [data collection rule (DCR)](transition-soc-optimization-recommendations#dcr-xdr-tables) in your workspace. If your content uses a `_CF` column, update it before you move it to Advanced Hunting.
+
+## Common update patterns
+
+Only a few schema patterns change between Microsoft Sentinel and Advanced Hunting. Update your content based on the patterns that apply to each table.
+
+### Pattern 1: Dynamic fields become strings
+
+This pattern applies to:
+
+- `DeviceEvents`
+- `DeviceFileEvents`
+- `DeviceProcessEvents`
+- `DeviceLogonEvents`
+- `DeviceNetworkEvents`
+- `DeviceInfo`
+- `EmailEvents`
+- `AlertEvidence`
+
+`AdditionalFields`, and `LoggedOnUsers` in `DeviceInfo`, are `dynamic` in Microsoft Sentinel but strings in Advanced Hunting.
+
+Before member access or `mv-expand`, parse the value by using `todynamic()` and `tostring()`.
+
+For example:
+
+```kusto
+DeviceInfo
+| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
+| extend Users = todynamic(tostring(LoggedOnUsers))
+| mv-expand Users
+| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = tostring(Users.UserName)
+```
+
+### Pattern 2: Dynamic array fields become strings
+
+This pattern applies to the following `DeviceNetworkInfo` fields:
+
+- `IPAddresses`
+- `DnsAddresses`
+- `ConnectedNetworks`
+- `DefaultGateways`
+
+Parse these fields before using `mv-expand` or accessing individual elements.
+
+For example:
+
+```kusto
+DeviceNetworkInfo
+| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
+| extend IPs = todynamic(tostring(IPAddresses))
+| mv-expand IPs
+| project Timestamp, DeviceName, IPAddress = tostring(IPs.IPAddress)
+```
+
+### Pattern 3: Port fields become integers
+
+This pattern applies to:
+
+- `IdentityLogonEvents`
+- `IdentityDirectoryEvents`
+- `IdentityQueryEvents`
+
+The `Port` and `DestinationPort` fields are strings in Microsoft Sentinel and integers in Advanced Hunting.
+
+For example, a Microsoft Sentinel query might use:
+
+```kusto
+| where Port == "3389" or DestinationPort == "445"
+```
+
+In Advanced Hunting, normalize the fields by using `toint()`:
+
+```kusto
+IdentityLogonEvents
+| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
+| where toint(Port) == 3389 or toint(DestinationPort) == 445
+```
+
+### Pattern 4: SecurityAlert splits into AlertInfo and AlertEvidence
+
+Microsoft Sentinel's `SecurityAlert` table doesn't have a single equivalent in Advanced Hunting.
+
+Alert data is split between:
+
+- `AlertInfo`, which contains one row per alert.
+- `AlertEvidence`, which contains one row per entity associated with an alert.
+
+The following fields map between the schemas:
+
+| `SecurityAlert`field | Advanced Hunting | Notes |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `SystemAlertId` | `AlertId` | Join key between `AlertInfo` and `AlertEvidence` |
+| `AlertName` | `Title` |  |
+| `ProviderName` | `ServiceSource` |  |
+| `Entities` | `AlertEvidence` rows | Join the tables instead of using `mv-expand` on `Entities` |
+
+Join `AlertInfo` and `AlertEvidence` on `AlertId` when you need alert information together with related entities.
+
+For example:
+
+```kusto
+AlertInfo
+| where Timestamp > ago(1h)
+| where Title == "Suspicious PowerShell"
+| join kind=inner (
+    AlertEvidence
+    | where Timestamp > ago(1h)
+) on AlertId
+| extend Fields = todynamic(tostring(AdditionalFields))
+| project Timestamp, AlertId, Title, Severity, ServiceSource, EntityType, DeviceId, AccountName
+```
+
+### Other column changes
+
+In addition to the changes that apply to all tables, some tables have renamed, removed, or retyped columns in Advanced Hunting. Column names are case-sensitive.
+
+| Table | Microsoft Sentinel | Advanced Hunting |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `CallActivityEvents` | `TimeGenerated` | `TimeGenerated` works and returns the same value as `ActivityTimestamp`. The table doesn't have a `Timestamp` column, so don't change `TimeGenerated` to `Timestamp`. In new queries, use `ActivityTimestamp`. |
+| `CallActivityEvents` | `OriginatorUserObjectId` | `OriginatorObjectId` |
+| `FileMaliciousContentInfo` | `DetectionMethods` (string) | `DetectionMethods` (dynamic) |
+| `EmailEvents` | `LastEventExecutionTime` | Not available. Remove this column from your queries. |
+| `EmailPostDeliveryEvents` | `ApproverUpn` | Not available in most tenants. Remove this column from your queries, or use `column_ifexists("ApproverUpn", "")`. |
+| `DeviceInfo` | `DeviceObjectId` | Not available. Remove this column from your queries. |
+| `AlertEvidence` | `AzureResourceId`, `AzureResourceType`, `AzureSubscriptionId` | `ResourceID`, `ResourceType`, `SubscriptionId` |
+| `DisruptionAndResponseEvents` | `DataSources` | `DataSource`. Queries that already use `DataSource` don't need to change. |
+| `DisruptionAndResponseEvents` | `InitiatingProcessId` (int) | `InitiatingProcessId` (long) |
+| `DisruptionAndResponseEvents` | `Port` (string) | `Port` (int) |
+| `DisruptionAndResponseEvents` | `ReportId` (string) | `ReportId` (long) |
+| `DisruptionAndResponseEvents` | `MachineGroup` | Present but always empty. Don't use it for filtering or scoping. |
+| `CloudAuditEvents` | `CloudResourceId` | Not available. Use `AzureResourceId`, `AwsResourceName`, or `GcpFullResourceName`. |
+| `CloudDnsEvents` | `ImageDigest`, `HostName`, `Region` | Might not be available. To check, run `CloudDnsEvents \| getschema` in Advanced Hunting. |
+| `CloudProcessEvents` | `ParentProcessId` (string), `InitiatingProcessId` (string) | `ParentProcessId` (long), `InitiatingProcessId` (long) |
+| `CloudProcessEvents` | `AdditionalFields` (string) | `AdditionalFields` (dynamic) |
+
+Some `CallActivityEvents` columns, including `OriginatorObjectId`, `CallType`, `CallName`, and the `ActivityRecipient` columns, are available in Advanced Hunting only if your organization has preview features turned on. Before you update content that uses these columns, run `CallActivityEvents | getschema` in Advanced Hunting to check which columns you have.
+
+This table reflects the schema that Advanced Hunting returns. If a column name or type differs from the table's schema reference page, run `<TableName> | getschema` in Advanced Hunting to confirm.
+
+## Validate your updates
+
+Before you stop ingestion in Microsoft Sentinel:
+
+1. **Update queries.** Update hunting and saved queries for the applicable parsing logic, port conversions, and alert joins.
+2. **Validate detections.** Confirm that analytics rules and custom detections return the expected results.
+3. **Validate workbooks.** Check tiles, filters, and parameters that reference changed columns or data types.
+4. **Validate automation.** Test playbooks, Logic Apps, and API integrations against the Advanced Hunting response format, and confirm Microsoft Defender permissions and workload scoping for automation identities.
+5. **Stop ingestion.** When all content is updated and validated, stop ingestion for the supported Defender XDR tables. For steps, see [Optimize Microsoft Defender XDR data ingestion](transition-optimize-xdr-ingestion).
\ No newline at end of file

englishSummary.headline: Guidance added for transitioning to Advanced Hunting tables
englishSummary.summary: The guidance identifies affected Defender XDR tables, column and data-type differences, and required updates for queries, detections, workbooks, and automation when transitioning Microsoft Sentinel content.
englishSummary.adminImpact: Administrators must update and validate dependent content before stopping ingestion for supported Defender XDR tables.

+# Tune alerts from migrated custom detections in Microsoft Defender | Microsoft Learn
+
+Create a temporary alert tuning rule to auto-resolve evaluation alerts while you validate migrated custom detections. Migrated custom detections use `#EVAL` in their alert titles during evaluation. Match both the detection source and the title so that the rule doesn't resolve unrelated alerts.
+
+Before you begin, review the access and Preview availability prerequisites.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- Access to **Settings > Microsoft Defender XDR > Alert tuning** in the Microsoft Defender portal.
+- **Custom detection** available in the **Detection source** list. Detection source selection is a Preview capability, and availability can differ between tenants. Create the rule only after this option appears.
+- Migrated custom detections under evaluation, with `#EVAL` in their alert titles.
+
+## Create the temporary tuning rule
+
+Use both matching conditions to restrict the rule to migrated custom detection evaluation alerts.
+
+Important
+
+Alert tuning can change alert visibility, incidents, notifications, and automation. Keep both conditions: **Detection source = Custom detection** and **Alert title** contains `#EVAL`. Don't use the title condition alone.
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Defender portal](https://security.microsoft.com).
+2. Go to **Settings > Microsoft Defender XDR > Alert tuning**.
+3. Select **Create alert tuning rule**.
+4. Configure the following values:
+
+    | Setting | Value |
+    | --- | --- |
+    | **Rule name** | Suppress migrated custom detection evaluation alerts |
+    | **Detection source** | **Custom detection** |
+    | **Condition** | **Alert title** contains `#EVAL` |
+    | **Action** | **Auto-resolve** |
+    | **Status** | Enabled only for the migration validation period |
+5. Review the scope, create the rule, and confirm that it's enabled.
+
+## Validate matching and incident behavior
+
+Matching alerts should be auto-resolved. Each is expected to create a resolved one-alert, or singleton, incident. Closed incidents aren't reopened or merged, so these evaluation alerts shouldn't correlate between migrated rules or into existing incidents. Validate this behavior in your tenant.
+
+1. **Positive test:** Confirm that a `#EVAL` custom-detection alert is auto-resolved and that its incident is resolved with that alert as its only alert.
+2. **Correlation test:** Generate alerts from two different `#EVAL` custom detections. Confirm that they remain in separate resolved singleton incidents and aren't added to an existing incident.
+3. **Title test:** Confirm that a custom-detection alert without `#EVAL` isn't auto-resolved by this rule.
+4. **Source test:** Confirm that an alert from another detection source isn't auto-resolved by this rule, even if its title contains `#EVAL`.
+
+## Remove the rule after validation
+
+When migration validation is complete, disable or delete the temporary tuning rule. If other migrated detections still use the same rule for evaluation, wait until their validation is complete.
\ No newline at end of file

+# Automatically migrate Microsoft Sentinel analytics rules to custom detections | Microsoft Learn
+
+Use the migration tool in Microsoft Defender SOC optimization to convert eligible Microsoft Sentinel analytics rules to custom detections. Migrate one rule, selected rules, or all eligible rules in a recommendation, then compare the results before completing migration.
+
+The original analytics rules remain enabled during migration and evaluation. You can edit custom detections while they're being evaluated; you don't need to complete migration to edit them. Complete migration only after the custom detections and dependent automation meet your requirements.
+
+Before you begin, review the access and validation prerequisites.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- Access to the relevant SOC optimization recommendation in the Microsoft Defender portal.
+- Permissions to view recommendations, migrate analytics rules, manage custom detections, and update dependent automation.
+- A review of the affected analytics rules, automation, and other dependencies before changing data ingestion or retention.
+- A plan to compare alert volume, timing, severity, titles, entities, scheduling, and downstream automation during evaluation.
+- Follow [Tune alerts from custom detections under evaluation](transition-custom-detections-alert-tuning).
+
+## Review the migration stages and statuses
+
+The migration process has three stages:
+
+- **Migration:** Create custom detections from eligible analytics rules.
+- **Validation:** Compare the custom detections with their original analytics rules. Edit the custom detections as needed and validate the changes while the originals remain enabled.
+- **Completion:** Complete migration and disable the original analytics rules. Completion isn't required to edit the custom detections.
+
+The portal displays each rule's eligibility or progress:
+
+| Status | Meaning | Next action |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| **Ready to migrate** | The analytics rule is eligible for automatic migration. | Select the rule and start migration. |
+| **Under evaluation** | Migration eligibility is being reassessed. | Wait for evaluation to finish, then select **Refresh**. |
+| **Migration isn't available** | The current migration flow can't convert the rule. | Download the report and follow [Resolve migration blockers](transition-custom-detections-migration-blockers). |
+| **In progress** | The tool is creating the custom detection. | Wait for processing to finish and refresh the status. |
+| **Validating** | The custom detection generates evaluation alerts while the original analytics rule stays enabled. | Compare behavior, edit the custom detection if needed, and validate before completion. |
+| **Completed** | Migration is complete, and the original analytics rule is disabled. | Confirm detection results and review remaining dependencies. |
+
+**Under evaluation** refers to migration eligibility checks. **Validating** refers to the period when you evaluate a migrated custom detection.
+
+## Open a SOC optimization recommendation
+
+Use the recommendation for the table whose ingestion you plan to change.
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Defender portal](https://security.microsoft.com).
+2. Go to **SOC optimization**.
+3. Open the relevant **Stop ingesting** recommendation.
+4. Select the **Analytic rules** tab.
+5. Review the migration summary and each rule's status.
+
+    ![Screenshot of the migration summary and analytics rules with ready and unavailable statuses.](media/transition-custom-detections-automatic/migration-summary.png)
+
+For a rule marked **Migration isn't available**, select **Download report**. Use [Resolve migration blockers](transition-custom-detections-migration-blockers) to match the report code to its resolution, validate any changes, and refresh eligibility. If no safe migration path is available, retain the original rule.
+
+## Migrate analytics rules
+
+Choose the migration scope that matches the rules you want to evaluate.
+
+Some JSON columns, including `DeviceEvents.AdditionalFields` and `DeviceNetworkInfo.ConnectedNetworks`, are `dynamic` in Log Analytics but JSON-formatted strings in advanced hunting. Parse the column with `todynamic()` before accessing a property or array element, for example, `todynamic(AdditionalFields).Property` or `todynamic(ConnectedNetworks)[0]`. Use `tostring()` when comparing extracted values with text. Migration applies this conversion automatically for scheduled analytics rules. For streaming (NRT) rules, direct nested access to affected columns is an eligibility blocker: update the source analytics-rule query, then reassess eligibility. Apply the same parsing when manually running the original query in advanced hunting. Validate changes against representative data in both environments; other schema differences and migration blockers can still require changes.
+
+The following table lists the affected JSON columns.
+
+| Table | Affected columns |
+| --- | --- |
+| `DeviceNetworkInfo` | `ConnectedNetworks`, `DefaultGateways`, `DnsAddresses`, `IPAddresses` |
+| `DeviceNetworkEvents` | `AdditionalFields` |
+| `DeviceProcessEvents` | `AdditionalFields` |
+| `DeviceInfo` | `AdditionalFields`, `LoggedOnUsers` |
+| `DeviceFileEvents` | `AdditionalFields` |
+| `DeviceLogonEvents` | `AdditionalFields` |
+| `DeviceEvents` | `AdditionalFields` |
+| `AlertEvidence` | `AdditionalFields` |
+| `EmailEvents` | `AdditionalFields` |
+
+Other columns can also have different schemas or query requirements.
+
+### Migrate a single rule
+
+Select one eligible analytics rule from the recommendation.
+
+1. In the recommendation's **Analytic rules** tab, find a rule marked **Ready to migrate**.
+2. Select its checkbox, or open its side panel.
+3. Select **Migrate rules** or **Migrate rule**, depending on the entry point.
+4. Review the migration confirmation.
+
+The tool creates a custom detection. After successful creation, the rule moves to **Validating**, and the original analytics rule stays enabled.
+
+### Migrate all eligible rules
+
+Use the migration tool to migrate all eligible rules in the recommendation.
+
+Important
+
+**Migrate now** starts migration for all eligible rules in the recommendation. Filtering the rule list doesn't narrow this scope. Rules marked **Migration isn't available** aren't included.
+
+1. Open the relevant **Stop ingesting** recommendation.
+2. Select **Open migration tool**.
+3. On **Get started**, review the migration, validation, and completion stages.
+4. Select **Migrate now**.
+
+## Monitor migration
+
+Check creation progress before evaluating the custom detections.
+
+1. Return to the recommendation where you started migration.
+2. Review each rule's status.
+3. Select **Refresh** to check the latest progress.
+
+During creation, the status is **In progress**. After successful creation, it changes to **Validating**. The custom detection generates evaluation alerts, and the original analytics rule remains enabled.
+
+Creating a custom detection doesn't complete migration. You explicitly complete migration for each rule after evaluation.
+
+## Evaluate and edit custom detections
+
+Compare each migrated custom detection with its original analytics rule over a representative period.
+
+Tip
+
+**Initial 30-day run:** When a custom detection is first created, it runs against the previous 30 days of data. This initial run can generate multiple alerts from historical matches. Account for these historical results when comparing alerts during evaluation.
+
+1. In the recommendation, select **Manage rules under validation**, or open the migration tool and select **Rules being validated**.
+2. Select the custom detections you want to evaluate.
+3. Compare alert volume, timing, severity, titles, entities, scheduling, and downstream automation.
+4. Edit a custom detection during evaluation if changes are needed.
+5. Validate the edited detection and its dependent automation before completing migration.
+
+    ![Screenshot of the migration validation panel with Complete migration and Cancel and delete actions.](media/transition-custom-detections-automatic/validation-panel.png)
+
+**Custom detections are editable during evaluation.** Leave a rule in **Validating** while you investigate or test changes. Rules in a bulk migration can be evaluated and completed independently.
+
+Evaluation alerts contain `#EVAL` in their titles. Use [Tune alerts from custom detections under evaluation](transition-custom-detections-alert-tuning) to auto-resolve only alerts that match both **Detection source = Custom detection** and **Alert title** contains `#EVAL`. Validate the tuning rule's scope and incident behavior before relying on it.
+
+Important
+
+Don't complete migration until detection results and downstream automation meet your requirements. Revalidate any edits made during evaluation.
+
+## Complete migration
+
+Complete migration only for custom detections that have passed evaluation, including any edits made during that period.
+
+1. In the recommendation, select **Manage rules under validation**.
+2. Select the custom detections that passed evaluation.
+3. Select **Complete migration**.
+4. Review the updated statuses.
+
+You can also complete migration from the custom detection page.
+
+When migration is complete:
+
+- The custom detection is enabled, and its migration status is **Completed**.
+- The original Microsoft Sentinel analytics rule is disabled.
+
+When validation is complete for all detections using the temporary tuning rule, disable or delete the alert tuning rule.
+
+Important
+
+Completing migration disables the original analytics rule. Verify the replacement and its dependent automation before proceeding.
+
+## Cancel migration
+
+If a custom detection isn't ready for completion, leave it in **Validating** while you investigate or edit it. To cancel its migration instead:
+
+1. Open **Manage rules under validation** in the recommendation.
+2. Select the custom detection.
+3. Select **Cancel and delete**.
+
+The migrated custom detection is deleted, and the original analytics rule remains enabled.
+
+## Verify migration results
+
+Confirm completed migrations and identify any remaining dependencies.
+
+1. Return to the recommendation and select **Analytic rules**.
+2. Confirm that successfully migrated rules show **Completed**.
+3. Review rules still marked **Ready to migrate**, **Under evaluation**, **Validating**, or **Migration isn't available**.
+
+    ![Screenshot of rule statuses showing completed migrations and a rule for which migration isn't available.](media/transition-custom-detections-automatic/migration-results.png)
+4. Resolve remaining rule and automation dependencies before changing ingestion or retention for the affected table.
+
+Important
+
+Completing some migrations doesn't mean all dependencies have been addressed. Check all analytics rules, automation, and other dependencies before reducing or stopping ingestion.
+
+## Compare alert properties after migration
+
+Alerts from migrated custom detections include compatibility values for existing Microsoft Sentinel flows. Some values differ between the Defender and Sentinel views.
+
+Both value columns below describe the **Sentinel view for workspaces onboarded to the Defender portal**. Optional properties depend on the information available for each alert. Use the table during evaluation and when updating downstream automation.
+
+| Property name | Change | Value for new custom detections | Value for custom detections migrated from analytics rules | Notes |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| `ProviderName` | Changed | `MicrosoftThreatProtection` (Defender XDR); `MDATP` (MDE-native) | `Microsoft Sentinel` |  |
+| `ProductComponentName` | Added | Not populated | `ASI Scheduled Alerts` (scheduled); `ASI NRT Alerts` (NRT) |  |
+| `ProductName` | Changed | `Microsoft Defender XDR` (XDR); `Microsoft Defender for Endpoint` (MDE-native); or a custom product name | `Azure Sentinel` | The migrated rule's product name is also `Azure Sentinel` in Defender for analytics rule alerts. |
+| `AlertType` | Changed | The custom detection detector ID | `<sourceWorkspaceId>_<sourceAnalyticRuleId>` |  |
+| `ExtendedProperties["Analytic Rule Ids"]` | Added | Not populated by default | Same value as in the matching analytics rule | Identifies the original analytics rule, not the custom detection rule or detector. |
+| `ExtendedProperties["Analytic Rule Name"]` | Added | Not populated by default | Same value as in the matching analytics rule | Separate from the generated alert title. |
+| `ExtendedProperties["MigratedAnalyticRule"]` | Added | Not populated by default | `"true"` |  |
+| `ExtendedProperties["Correlation Id"]` | Added | Not populated by default | The rule execution (run) ID | Identifies an execution, not an alert ID. |
+| `ExtendedProperties["Query Start Time UTC"]` / `ExtendedProperties["Query End Time UTC"]` | Added | Not populated by default | Same value as in the matching analytics rule | Different from the alert's activity start and end times. |
+| `ExtendedProperties["Query Period"]` | Added | Not populated by default | Same value as in the matching analytics rule |  |
+| `ExtendedProperties["Trigger Operator"]` / `ExtendedProperties["Trigger Threshold"]` | Added | Not populated by default | Same value as in the matching analytics rule |  |
+| `ExtendedProperties["Event Grouping"]` | Added | Not populated by default | Same value as in the matching analytics rule | Describes how alerts are generated, not how incidents are grouped. |
+| `ExtendedProperties["Search Query Results Overall Count"]` | Added | Not populated by default | Same value as in the matching analytics rule | Don't assume a total result count is available for grouped alerts. |
+| `ExtendedProperties["Data Sources"]` | Added | Not populated by default | Same value as in the matching analytics rule |  |
+| `ExtendedProperties["Query"]` | Not yet available | Not populated by default | Not available yet | This field isn't available on alerts from migrated custom detections. |
+| `ExtendedProperties["OriginalQuery"]` | Not yet available | Not populated by default | Not available yet | This field isn't available on alerts from migrated custom detections. |
+
+## Troubleshoot migration
+
+Use the status and report to choose the next action.
+
+| Issue | Next action |
+| --- | --- |
+| **Migrate rules** is unavailable. | Select at least one rule marked **Ready to migrate**. If eligibility checks are running, wait and select **Refresh**. |
+| A rule shows **Migration isn't available**. | Select **Download report** and follow [Resolve migration blockers](transition-custom-detections-migration-blockers). Preserve detection intent when editing or redesigning the rule. |
+| Migration remains **In progress**. | Select **Refresh**. If migration fails, review the reported error before retrying. |
+| A custom detection needs changes. | Edit it during evaluation, then validate the detection and dependent automation again. You don't need to complete migration to edit it. |
+| A custom detection isn't ready for completion. | Leave it in **Validating**, or use **Cancel and delete**. The original analytics rule remains enabled until completion. |

+
+# Troubleshoot Microsoft Sentinel analytics rule migration blockers | Microsoft Learn
+
+When an analytics rule shows **Migration isn't available**, use its migration report to identify the blocker. Match the report code to the guidance, decide whether a change is safe, and validate the rule before reassessing eligibility.
+
+Before editing a rule, review the access, backup, and validation prerequisites.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- Permissions to edit analytics rules and manage custom detections.
+- An exported or copied rule configuration that you can restore.
+- A representative validation period and expected test events.
+- A list of automation rules, playbooks, workbooks, and integrations that depend on the current alerts.
+
+Important
+
+Rule changes can affect alert volume, timing, entities, incidents, and automation. Don't change a rule only to get migration eligibility. Keep the original analytics rule enabled until migration is explicitly completed. Validate every change, and retain the original behavior when the operational risk is greater than the benefit of migrating now.
+
+## Troubleshooting checklist
+
+Identify the reported blocker and the safest next action before editing.
+
+### Download and match the report
+
+Use the latest report to identify the blocker and assess a safe resolution.
+
+1. In the SOC optimization recommendation, select **Download report** for rules marked **Migration isn't available**.
+2. Match the error code or message to the blocker index.
+3. Record the current rule configuration and expected behavior.
+4. Decide whether to edit the rule, evaluate a separate redesign, or retain it until a supported migration path is available.
+
+### Validate source-rule changes
+
+Test the edited analytics rule before requesting reassessment.
+
+1. Change one blocker at a time when practical.
+2. Save the edited analytics rule and validate that it still detects the intended activity.
+3. Compare alert volume, timing, entities, incident behavior, and dependent automation.
+4. Reassess eligibility only after the changes preserve detection intent.
+
+## Causes and solutions
+
+Use the exact report code to find the relevant category. Match the report wording below to the message in your downloaded report. Values in braces are placeholders. A rule can have more than one blocker.
+
+| Blocker | Report code |
+| --- | --- |
+| Dynamic alert properties | `UnsupportedAlertDetailsOverride`, `UnsupportedAlertProperty`, `InvalidDynamicProperties` |
+| Unsupported entity type | `UnsupportedEntityType` |
+| Unsupported Sentinel entities mapping | `UnsupportedSentinelEntitiesMapping` |
+| Alerts without incidents | `UnsupportedIncidentConfiguration` |
+| Secondary workspace | `NonPrimaryLogAnalyticsWorkspace` |
+| Cross-workspace query | `CrossWorkspaceCustomDetectionNotSupported` |
+| NRT watchlist | `NrtFunctionsNotSupported` |
+| NRT multiple tables | `NrtMultipleTablesNotSupported` |
+| NRT workspace operator | `NrtCrossWorkspaceNotSupported` |
+| Other streaming failure | `NrtStreamingIncompatible`, `NrtStreamingCompatibilityUnknown` |
+| NRT externaldata | `NrtExternalDataNotSupported` |
+| NRT event grouping | `UnsupportedNrtSingleAlertGrouping` |
+| ASIM, custom, or nested functions | `UnsupportedLogAnalyticsCustomFunction`, `NrtFunctionsNotSupported`, `HuntingRuleWithPrivateFunction`, `HuntingRuleQuerySyntaxErrors` |
+| Suppression | `UnsupportedSuppression` |
+| Non-default threshold | `UnsupportedThreshold` |
+
+### Dynamic alert properties and alert-details overrides
+
+**Report codes:**`UnsupportedAlertDetailsOverride`, `UnsupportedAlertProperty`, `InvalidDynamicProperties`.
+
+**Report wording:** The Analytics Rule overrides dynamic alert details; Custom Detections have no equivalent override.
+
+**Resolution:** Remove the dynamic alert-details overrides, retaining values analysts need as custom details. If several static values are required, splitting the rule is a redesign to validate before adoption. Apply changes only when they preserve detection intent.
+
+### Unsupported entity type
+
+**Report code:**`UnsupportedEntityType`.
+
+**Report wording:** The rule contains an entity type that is not supported by custom detections. Unsupported AnalyticsEntityType: {value}
+
+**Resolution:** Replace the unsupported mapping with a supported entity type that carries the same information. Remove the mapping only if investigation and automation don't need it.
+
+### Unsupported Sentinel entities mapping
+
+**Report code:**`UnsupportedSentinelEntitiesMapping`.
+
+**Report wording:** The rule uses Sentinel prebuilt entity mappings that are not supported by custom detection alert creation.
+
+**Resolution:** Replace the prebuilt mapping with explicit, supported entity mappings taken from the query results.
+
+### Alerts without incidents
+
+**Report code:**`UnsupportedIncidentConfiguration`.
+
+**Report wording:** The Analytics Rule has custom incident configuration; Custom Detections have no incident configuration equivalent.
+
+**Resolution:** If the behavior change is acceptable, enable incident creation with the default settings. Use Defender alert tuning or automation rules if incidents should be auto-resolved or hidden. Validate the changed incident behavior and dependent automation before migration.
+
+### Rule runs on a secondary workspace
+
+**Report code:**`NonPrimaryLogAnalyticsWorkspace`.
+
+**Report wording:** Custom Detections that query Log Analytics tables can only be created on the tenant's primary workspace.
+
+**Resolution:** Recreate the rule against equivalent data in the primary workspace. Keep the original enabled until the replacement is validated. If equivalent data isn't available locally, retain the rule in Sentinel.
+
+### Cross-workspace query using workspace()
+
+**Report code:**`CrossWorkspaceCustomDetectionNotSupported`.
+
+**Report wording:** This Analytics Rule references multiple workspaces ({WorkspaceIds}). Custom Detections require a single workspace. Rewrite the query to use one workspace and try again.
+
+**Resolution:** Replace every `workspace()` call with equivalent local tables, or split the rule and retain the remote-data logic in Sentinel.
+
+### NRT rule uses a watchlist
+
+**Report code:**`NrtFunctionsNotSupported`.
+
+**Report wording:** This NRT Analytics Rule references query functions ({FunctionNames}). Streaming Custom Detections do not support function references. Rewrite the query using supported KQL without functions and try again.
+
+**Resolution:** Remove the watchlist lookup only if detection intent is preserved. If the lookup is essential, change the rule to a scheduled analytics rule before migration.
+
+### NRT rule queries multiple tables
+
+**Report code:**`NrtMultipleTablesNotSupported`.
+
+**Report wording:** This NRT Analytics Rule references multiple tables ({DistinctTableNames}); streaming Custom Detections require a single table. Rewrite the query to use one table and try again.
+
+**Resolution:** Rewrite the query to use one table, or split it into single-table detections. If the cross-table logic is essential, use a scheduled analytics rule.
+
+### NRT rule uses the workspace operator
+
+**Report code:**`NrtCrossWorkspaceNotSupported`.
+
+**Report wording:** This NRT Analytics Rule references multiple workspaces ({WorkspaceIds}). Streaming Custom Detections require a single workspace. Rewrite the query to use one workspace and try again.
+
+**Resolution:** Replace each `workspace()` call with the equivalent local table, or retain the remote-data logic in a separate Sentinel rule.
+
+### Other streaming failure
+
+**Report codes:**`NrtStreamingIncompatible`, `NrtStreamingCompatibilityUnknown`.
+
+**Report wording for NrtStreamingIncompatible:** The NRT Analytics Rule could not be validated as compatible with streaming Custom Detections. {StreamingCompatibilityReason}
+
+**Report wording for NrtStreamingCompatibilityUnknown:** Streaming compatibility could not be determined for this NRT Analytics Rule; migration requires a confirmed compatible query.
+
+**Resolution:** Simplify the query to single-table streaming KQL without functions, joins, unions, or external references. If the required logic can't be preserved, use a scheduled analytics rule.
+
+### NRT query uses externaldata
+
+**Report code:**`NrtExternalDataNotSupported`.
+
+**Report wording:** This NRT Analytics Rule uses the externaldata operator, which is not supported in streaming Custom Detections. Remove the externaldata reference and try again.
+
+**Resolution:** Write the external data values directly into the query filter, or use a scheduled analytics rule if the external data is essential.
+
+### NRT rule uses event grouping
+
+**Report code:**`UnsupportedNrtSingleAlertGrouping`.
+
+**Report wording:** NRT Custom Detections don't support grouping all query results into a single alert.
+
+**Resolution:** Switch the rule to one alert per event only when that behavior is acceptable. If events need to be grouped into a single alert, use a scheduled analytics rule.
+
+### ASIM, custom, or nested functions
+
+**Report codes:**`UnsupportedLogAnalyticsCustomFunction`, `NrtFunctionsNotSupported`, `HuntingRuleWithPrivateFunction`, `HuntingRuleQuerySyntaxErrors`.
+
+**Report wording:** This Analytics Rule uses the Log Analytics custom function '{FunctionName}'. Custom functions aren't currently supported for migration to Custom Detections. Inline the function logic in the rule query and try again.
+
+**Resolution:** Inline the logic of every custom, ASIM, or nested function so that the rule query no longer calls saved functions. Validate that the rewritten query preserves the intended behavior.
+
+### Suppression is enabled
+
+**Report code:**`UnsupportedSuppression`.
+
+**Report wording:** The Analytics Rule uses alert suppression; Custom Detections have no suppression equivalent.
+
+**Resolution:** Turn off **Stop running query after alert is generated** only when the change is acceptable. Handle noise with KQL aggregation, alert tuning, or automation, and validate the resulting alert volume.
+
+### Non-default trigger threshold
+
+**Report code:**`UnsupportedThreshold`.
+
+**Report wording:** The Analytics Rule only alerts after {N} matches ({Operator}); Custom Detections have no threshold equivalent. A structural conversion can instead return: Unsupported AlertTriggerOperator: {value}.
+
+**Resolution:** Move the threshold into the query by aggregating and filtering. Then set the alert threshold to **greater than 0** and validate the results.
+
+## Reassess eligibility
+
+Eligibility refresh isn't instant. After saving and validating changes:
+
+1. Return to the SOC optimization recommendation and open **Analytic rules**.
+2. Select **Refresh** and wait while the rule shows **Under evaluation**.
+3. If the rule becomes **Ready to migrate**, select it and follow the [single-rule or bulk migration flow](transition-custom-detections-automatic#migrate-analytics-rules).
+4. If **Migration isn't available** remains, download a new report and resolve the next blocker.
+5. Repeat the edit, validation, and reassessment cycle until the rule is ready or you choose to retain it in Sentinel.
+
+## Review unresolved issues
+
+Use the following checks if eligibility or detection behavior doesn't match expectations.
+
+| Issue | Next action |
+| --- | --- |
+| The rule is still unavailable. | Download a new report because another blocker might remain. |
+| The rule stays **Under evaluation**. | Wait, select **Refresh**, and confirm that the saved rule and workspace match the recommendation. |
+| Alert volume increased after editing. | Restore the original configuration or tune the query before migration. |
+| Entity or incident quality degraded. | Restore the stronger mapping or incident behavior and retain the rule until support is available. |
+| The rewritten query produces different results. | Compare parameters, functions, time filters, joins, projected columns, and result schema. |
+| Required data isn't available locally. | Retain the rule in Sentinel. A rule edit doesn't resolve the data-availability constraint. |
