+# Manually convert Microsoft Sentinel analytics rules to custom detections | Microsoft Learn
+
+When you transition to using Microsoft Defender XDR data directly, you can convert Microsoft Sentinel analytics rules to Microsoft Defender custom detections.
+
+For eligible analytics rules identified in SOC optimization recommendations, you can use the [automatic migration tool](transition-custom-detections-automatic). For rules that aren't eligible for automatic migration, or when you need to recreate rules outside the supported migration workflow, follow the guidance in this article to convert them manually.
+
+Some analytics rule capabilities work differently in custom detections and require changes to the rule configuration or query. Other capabilities don't have direct custom detection equivalents and might require you to redesign the detection scenario.
+
+Before you retire an analytics rule, review the differences described in this article and validate the replacement custom detection.
+
+## Differences between analytics rules and custom detections
+
+The following table summarizes the main differences to consider when converting analytics rules to custom detections.
+
+| Area | What changes | Custom detection support |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Rule scheduling and execution | Microsoft Defender XDR-based rules use fixed frequency and lookback options. | Partial |
+| Alerts, incidents, and correlation | Grouping and correlation are handled centrally and are based on mapped entities instead of per-rule configuration. | Partial |
+| Automation, tuning, and suppression | Recreate automation by using alert-triggered automation. Handle tuning and suppression in the query or through automation. | Partial |
+| Detection queries and functions | Recreate custom functions in Advanced Hunting. Nested functions and cross-workspace queries aren't supported. | Partial |
+| Alert content and entities | Custom detections support one tactic and one identifier per entity. Dynamic values are supported for alert titles and descriptions. | Partial |
+| Multi-workspace and MSSP scenarios | Custom detections don't support cross-workspace queries, secondary-workspace detections, or query isolation. | Not supported |
+| Monitoring, health, and auditing | Use custom detection run status and `CloudAppEvents` audit data instead of Microsoft Sentinel health data and workbooks. | Partial |
+| Managing rules programmatically | Custom detection APIs and Bicep support are in preview. Existing analytics rules and ARM templates can't be imported directly as custom detections. New Content Hub solutions can include custom detection counterparts to analytics rules. | Preview |
+
+## Update rule scheduling and execution
+
+When you recreate an analytics rule as a custom detection, review its scheduling, execution, and near-real-time configuration.
+
+| Analytics rule capability | In custom detections | What to do |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Frequency from 5 minutes to 14 days | Supported scheduling options are **Continuous (NRT)**, **Hourly**, **Every 3 hours**, **Every 12 hours**, and **Every 24 hours**. | Recreate the rule by using the closest supported frequency. |
+| Flexible lookback | The lookback period is automatically determined by the selected frequency. For example, an hourly detection evaluates the previous four hours of data. | Select the closest supported frequency. The corresponding lookback window is applied automatically. |
+| Near-real-time (NRT) | Continuous detections support only specific single-table queries and a limited set of KQL operators. | If the query and tables are supported, use **Continuous (NRT)**. Otherwise, use a scheduled detection. |
+| NRT with enrichment, such as watchlists | Continuous detections use a limited KQL set, so lookups can't run as part of a continuous detection. | Remove the enrichment to use a continuous detection, or keep the enrichment and use a scheduled detection. |
+| Delayed first run | Custom detections don't provide start-time control. When you save a custom detection, it initially evaluates the previous 30 days of data and then continues at the selected frequency. | Plan for the initial evaluation and any alerts it might generate. |
+| On-demand rerun over a previous time window | Custom detections don't support arbitrary reruns. Each run evaluates the predefined lookback associated with the selected frequency. | Use the default lookback. Late-arriving events are evaluated automatically and duplicate alerts are prevented. |
+
+## Review alert grouping and incident correlation
+
+Microsoft Defender handles alert grouping and incident correlation centrally by using the entities, assets, and evidence associated with alerts.
+
+When converting an analytics rule, consider the following differences:
+
+- **Automatic event grouping**: Custom detections can group and deduplicate related events. Events that share the same assets and evidence might be combined into a single alert.
+- **One alert for all matching events**: Custom detections don't provide a rule setting that explicitly generates one alert for all matching events. Grouping is determined by the Microsoft Defender correlation engine.
+- **Correlation configuration**: Settings for excluding alerts from correlation, creating alerts without incidents, and configuring alert or incident grouping don't have direct equivalents in custom detections. Correlation uses mapped entities to group related alerts and incidents.
+- **Alert thresholds**: Custom detections don't provide a rule-level alert threshold. Add threshold logic directly to the KQL query instead.
+
+For example, the following query generates results only when an account has more than five failed sign-in events:
+
+```kusto
+DeviceLogonEvents
+| where Timestamp > ago(1h)
+| where ActionType == "LogonFailed"
+| summarize FailedCount = count() by AccountName, DeviceName
+| where FailedCount > 5
+```
+
+## Recreate automation, tuning, and suppression
+
+Recreate automation by using alert-triggered automation in Microsoft Defender. Handle tuning and suppression through KQL filtering and automation instead of analytics rule settings.
+
+Consider the following differences:
+
+- **Alert-triggered automation and playbooks**: After you create the custom detection, recreate any required alert-triggered automation in Microsoft Defender.
+- **Incident automation based on a rule**: You can't currently use a custom detection as a condition in an incident-triggered automation rule.
+- **In-rule suppression**: Custom detections don't have a direct equivalent to the analytics rule **Stop running query after alert is generated** behavior. Reduce noise by refining the detection query and using automation to resolve known-benign alerts.
+- **Alert tuning and suppression rules**: Custom detection alerts don't currently have a direct equivalent. Use query filtering and automation-based resolution where needed.
+
+## Update detection queries and functions
+
+Custom detections run against Advanced Hunting data and use Advanced Hunting functions.
+
+Review the following query differences when converting a rule:
+
+- **ASIM parsers**: Built-in unifying parsers, such as `_Im_<schema>`, can be used directly in custom detection queries.
+- **Custom functions**: Recreate Microsoft Sentinel workspace functions as Advanced Hunting functions and save them under **Shared functions** or **My functions**. Functions stored only in the Microsoft Sentinel workspace aren't available to custom detections.
+- **Cross-workspace queries**: The `workspace()` operator isn't supported. Rewrite the query to use local Advanced Hunting tables. If the required data isn't available locally, redesign the detection or continue using the analytics rule.
+- **Nested functions**: Advanced Hunting functions can't call other functions. Combine nested function logic into a single function or directly into the detection query.
+- **Function scope**: After a function is used by a custom detection, you can't modify the function to broaden its data scope. Create a new function instead.
+
+## Recreate alert content and entity mappings
+
+Review MITRE ATT&CK mappings, entity identifiers, and dynamic alert content when you recreate a rule.
+
+- **MITRE ATT&CK mapping**: Custom detections support one tactic per rule. Select the most relevant tactic, or create separate custom detections when different tactics need to be represented.
+- **Entity identifiers**: Custom detections map one query column per entity type. If an analytics rule maps multiple identifiers for the same entity, recreate the required mappings individually.
+- **Dynamic alert properties**: Custom detections support dynamic values in the alert title and description. You can reference up to three query columns in each field by using `{{Column}}`.
+- **Additional runtime values**: Add other values returned by the query as **Custom details**.
+
+For example:
+
+```text
+Alert title:
+User {{AccountName}} signed in from {{Location}}
+
+Custom details:
+SignInCount = TotalSignIns
+```
+
+Custom details support up to 20 key-value pairs and a maximum of 4 KB per alert.
+
+## Review multi-workspace scenarios
+
+Custom detections don't provide direct equivalents for some Microsoft Sentinel multi-workspace scenarios.
+
+Before converting a rule, determine whether it depends on:
+
+- Cross-workspace queries that use `workspace()`.
+- Data that is available only in a secondary Microsoft Sentinel workspace.
+- Query isolation or similar MSSP-specific behavior.
+
+If the required data isn't available to Advanced Hunting in the tenant, redesign the detection scenario or keep the existing analytics rule.
+
+## Monitor custom detection health and auditing
+
+Monitoring for custom detections differs from analytics rule monitoring in Microsoft Sentinel.
+
+- **Rule health**: Review run status and execution details in the custom detection experience. Custom detections don't provide an equivalent Microsoft Sentinel health-log history or Advanced Hunting health table.
+- **Rule audit trail**: Custom detection audit information is available in the `CloudAppEvents` table. Use this data for reporting, investigations, or detections that monitor rule changes.
+- **Health and quality workbooks**: Microsoft Sentinel health workbooks don't monitor custom detections. Use the custom detection health experience and `CloudAppEvents` audit data instead.
+
+For example:
+
+```kusto
+CloudAppEvents
+| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
+| where ActionType has "detection" or ActionType has "rule"
+| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, ActionType, RawEventData
+```
+
+## Manually convert and validate analytics rules
+
+If you can't migrate an analytics rule automatically, recreate it as a custom detection and validate its behavior before retiring the original rule.
+
+Before converting a rule, verify that it doesn't depend on functionality without a direct custom detection equivalent, such as cross-workspace queries, secondary-workspace detections, correlation opt-out, alerts without incidents, or query isolation.
+
+To manually convert and validate an analytics rule:
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Defender portal](https://security.microsoft.com).
+2. Recreate the rule as a custom detection from Advanced Hunting or from the custom detection experience. Rewrite any `workspace()` or nested-function logic first.
+3. Reproduce the entity mappings. Map one identifier per entity type. If the analytics rule used multiple identifiers for an entity, recreate each required mapping.
+4. Rebuild the alert content. Recreate dynamic alert titles and descriptions, and move other runtime values to **Custom details**.
+5. Recreate any required alert-triggered automation in Microsoft Defender.
+6. Run the KQL query in Advanced Hunting and validate the results, entity mappings, alert content, frequency, and lookback period.
+7. After the custom detection is validated, disable the original analytics rule.
+8. Remove the analytics rule when you're confident that the replacement custom detection is working as expected.
+
+## Manage converted rules programmatically
+
+If your organization manages detections as code or at scale, review the automation and deployment processes that currently manage Microsoft Sentinel analytics rules.
+
+- **CI/CD pipelines**: Update source-control and deployment pipelines so they can deploy and manage custom detections and Advanced Hunting-based content.
+- **Infrastructure as code and import/export**: Current custom detection automation capabilities depend on the preview API. Analytics rule ARM templates can't be imported directly into custom detections. The automatic migration tool provides a separate conversion workflow for eligible rules. Otherwise, recreate the rules by using the custom detection experience or API.
+- **Rule-template API**: Custom detections don't have an equivalent to the Microsoft Sentinel Analytics Rules template catalog API (`alertRuleTemplates`).
+- **Create rules from Content Hub**: New Content Hub solutions can include custom detection counterparts to Microsoft Sentinel analytics rules. When a solution includes supported custom detections, they're installed as part of the solution deployment. For existing analytics rules that don't have a custom detection counterpart, use the automatic migration tool when eligible, or recreate the required detections manually.
\ No newline at end of file

+# Transition an existing Microsoft Sentinel deployment to ISOC | Microsoft Learn
+
+If you already use Microsoft Sentinel, you can opt in your existing Microsoft Sentinel deployment to Integrated Security Operations Center (ISOC) in Microsoft Defender.
+
+Before you opt in, complete the required prerequisites and review the content and integrations that depend on your existing Microsoft Sentinel data.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- Review the [ISOC eligibility and workspace requirements](/en-us/defender-xdr/isoc-overview).
+- Identify all Microsoft Sentinel workspaces that are part of your deployment.
+- Have the required [permissions to connect Microsoft Sentinel workspaces to the Microsoft Defender portal](microsoft-sentinel-onboard#microsoft-sentinel-prerequisites).
+- Identify the primary Microsoft Sentinel workspace that you plan to use with ISOC.
+
+## Review transition limitations
+
+ISOC is in preview. Capabilities and availability might change during the preview period. Before you opt in, review these limitations:
+
+- The transition converts all Microsoft Sentinel workspaces in your tenant to ISOC. The process is permanent and can't be undone.
+- Customers who onboarded to the Microsoft Sentinel data lake before September 23, 2026, can't currently opt in to ISOC.
+
+## Review billing changes before transitioning to ISOC
+
+After transitioning to ISOC, your invoice shows ISOC charges instead of Microsoft Sentinel charges. Review the following billing changes:
+
+- **Existing discounts:** Discounts negotiated for Microsoft Sentinel don't carry over to ISOC. Work with your Microsoft account team to review applicable discounts for ISOC before transitioning.
+- **Commitment tiers:** ISOC doesn't offer commitment-tier pricing.
+- **Microsoft 365 data benefit:** The Microsoft 365 data ingestion benefit of 5 MB per user per day doesn't apply to ISOC usage.
+- **Dedicated clusters:** If your workspace is linked to a dedicated cluster, you can continue to use its functionality. However, ISOC usage is billed separately and doesn't count toward your existing dedicated cluster commitment. You continue to be charged for any unused cluster commitment.
+
+## Connect all Microsoft Sentinel workspaces to the Defender portal
+
+Before opting in to ISOC, connect every Microsoft Sentinel workspace in your deployment to the unified security operations experience in the Microsoft Defender portal.
+
+**Required permissions:** **User Access Administrator** or **Microsoft Sentinel Contributor** with subscription **Owner** rights. Multi-workspace onboarding of a primary workspace requires **Global Administrator** or **Security Administrator** permissions.
+
+1. In the [Microsoft Defender portal](https://security.microsoft.com), go to **System** > **Settings** > **Microsoft Sentinel**.
+2. Select **Connect a workspace** and connect all remaining Microsoft Sentinel workspaces.
+3. Choose your primary workspace, review the changes, and complete the connection.
+
+For more information, see [Connect Microsoft Sentinel to the Microsoft Defender portal](microsoft-sentinel-onboard).
+
+## Align table retention to supported ISOC values
+
+ISOC supports specific retention values. Update tables configured with unsupported values, such as 120 or 150 days, before transitioning to ISOC. Aligning retention settings helps reduce the risk of unexpected billing changes.
+
+**Required permissions:** Workspace-level **Owner**, **Contributor**, or **Log Analytics Contributor** permissions to modify table retention.
+
+1. Go to **Setup & Configuration** > **Data Management** > **Data & Connectors** > **Tables**.
+2. Identify tables with unsupported retention values.
+3. Update each affected table to a supported value, such as 90 or 180 days for Microsoft Defender XDR scenarios.
+4. Repeat for all Microsoft Sentinel workspaces.
+
+Note
+
+ISOC includes 90 days of default retention for eligible tables and supports retention of 180 days and beyond for Microsoft Defender data. Retention beyond 90 days and up to 180 days is billed at the 180-day retention rate.
+
+## Import Microsoft Sentinel roles into Defender RBAC
+
+Microsoft Sentinel role assignments don't automatically transfer to Microsoft Defender role-based access control (RBAC). Importing existing roles helps preserve analyst and engineering access, simplifies permission management, and reduces the need to manually recreate role assignments. Skipping this step might result in some users losing access to Microsoft Defender data after conversion.
+
+**Required permissions:** **Security Administrator** or **Global Administrator** permissions.
+
+1. Open **Import roles** during the ISOC onboarding process.
+2. Review the preselected roles from your primary workspace.
+3. Review users, groups, and permissions, resolve any import errors, and complete the role import.
+
+For more information, see [Update permissions and roles with Unified RBAC](transition-unified-rbac).
+
+## Activate Defender RBAC workloads
+
+Imported role assignments only take effect after you [activate Defender RBAC for the relevant workloads](/en-us/defender-xdr/activate-defender-rbac). If you skip activation, imported roles remain inactive and users might not have their intended access.
+
+**Required permissions:** **Security Administrator** or **Global Administrator** permissions.
+
+1. Select **Activate workloads** during the ISOC onboarding process.
+2. Activate Defender RBAC for workloads that aren't yet enabled.
+3. Verify that key users and groups have the expected access.
+
+For tenants with multiple workspaces, this experience only applies to the primary workspace. For any secondary workspace containing Microsoft Defender tables, assign roles to the relevant users manually.
+
+For more information, see [Update permissions and roles with Unified RBAC](transition-unified-rbac).
+
+## Update content to use Microsoft Defender data
+
+After transitioning to ISOC, Microsoft Defender data is no longer duplicated into Microsoft Sentinel workspace tables in the same way.
+
+Review SOC optimization recommendations to update existing detections, workbooks, and automation to use Microsoft Defender advanced hunting data. These updates help maintain security coverage while reducing duplicate Microsoft Defender data ingestion costs. Don't reduce ingestion until you validate dependent content.
+
+**Required permissions:** Defender RBAC permissions for detection tuning and security data access, plus **Microsoft Sentinel Contributor** permissions where applicable.
+
+1. Go to **SOC optimization** and review recommendations under **Lower Defender data costs**. For more information about the recommendations, see the [SOC optimization reference](soc-optimization/soc-optimization-reference).
+2. For each recommendation, update queries, analytics rules, workbooks, and playbooks to use Microsoft Defender advanced hunting data for the affected table.
+3. Before reducing ingestion for each affected table, validate that:
+
+    - Advanced hunting queries return expected results.
+    - Detections generate the expected alerts.
+    - Workbooks display accurate data.
+    - Playbooks and automation execute successfully.
+    - Users and automation identities retain the required access.
+    - CI/CD pipelines reference the correct tables and schemas.
+
+Update and validate dependent content before ingestion changes. If ingestion changes first, detections, workbooks, automation, and other content might continue to reference data that is no longer arriving in the Microsoft Sentinel workspace.
+
+Work through the transition table by table instead of updating all affected content at once.
+
+For more information, see [Review SOC optimization recommendations](transition-soc-optimization-recommendations).
+
+## Stop duplicate Microsoft Defender data ingestion where applicable
+
+ISOC includes 90 days of default retention for eligible Microsoft Defender data at no additional cost. Review SOC optimization recommendations to stop duplicate ingestion into Microsoft Sentinel workspaces while preserving investigation and analysis capabilities through Microsoft Defender advanced hunting.
+
+Only stop duplicate ingestion after validating that dependent detections, workbooks, and automation have been updated. Stopping ingestion prematurely can create security coverage gaps.
+
+**Required permissions:** Workspace-level Azure RBAC write permissions, such as **Log Analytics Contributor**, **Contributor**, or **Owner**.
+
+1. Go to **Setup & Configuration** > **Data Management** > **Data & Connectors** > **Tables**.
+2. Select **Configure workspace** to stop streaming all eligible Microsoft Defender tables.
+
+    ![Screenshot of the Tables page showing Configure workspace to prepare the workspace for an ISOC upgrade.](media/transition-existing-sentinel-deployment/configure-workspace.png)
+3. If you have multiple workspaces, repeat this step for each workspace.
+
+For information about supported data, included retention, and additional ingestion charges, see [Data ingestion, retention, and billing for ISOC in Microsoft Defender](/en-us/defender-xdr/integrated-security-operations-data-billing-retention).
+
+Note
+
+ISOC includes 90 days of default retention for eligible tables and supports retention of 180 days and beyond for Microsoft Defender data. Retention beyond 90 days and up to 180 days is billed at the 180-day retention rate.
+
+## Review MSSP considerations
+
+If your Microsoft Sentinel deployment is managed by a managed security service provider (MSSP), review the deployment and delegation changes that apply before completing the transition.
+
+For more information, see [Transition MSSP-managed deployments to Microsoft Defender](transition-mssp-deployments).
+
+## Review what changes when you move to ISOC
+
+Review the changes that apply to your deployment:
+
+- **Tenant-wide transition:** All Microsoft Sentinel workspaces in your tenant transition to ISOC together. A combination of ISOC and non-ISOC workspaces isn't supported.
+- **Pricing and billing:** ISOC pricing and billing meters replace applicable Microsoft Sentinel pricing and meters. Review the discount, commitment-tier, and benefit changes described earlier with your Microsoft account team, and renegotiate discounts before transitioning.
+- **Data retention:** ISOC introduces 90-day default retention benefits and new pricing. Review your existing retention settings.
+- **Security operations:** Your workspaces become part of ISOC. Some existing detections, queries, workbooks, and automation might require updates.
\ No newline at end of file

+# Update Logic App playbook automation - Microsoft Sentinel | Microsoft Learn
+
+When you transition Microsoft Sentinel content from workspace-based data to Microsoft Defender XDR Advanced Hunting data, update Logic App playbooks that run Log Analytics queries so that they query Advanced Hunting instead.
+
+The update changes the query data source and response format while preserving the rest of the automation flow where possible. Typically, the playbook trigger and downstream enrichment, notification, or response actions remain the same.
+
+Note
+
+This article applies to Logic App playbooks that query Log Analytics or Azure Monitor Logs. It doesn't describe the migration of automation rules associated with Microsoft Sentinel analytics rules. For analytics rule migration, see [Convert Microsoft Sentinel analytics rules to custom detections](transition-custom-detections).
+
+For changes to KQL table names, time columns, and data types, see [Update Microsoft Sentinel content to use Advanced Hunting tables](transition-advanced-hunting-tables).
+
+## Understand the playbook changes
+
+The following table summarizes the main changes when you update a playbook to use Advanced Hunting.
+
+| Current implementation | Target implementation |
+| --- | --- |
+| Log Analytics or Azure Monitor Logs connector | Microsoft Graph API call to Advanced Hunting |
+| Workspace-based Microsoft Sentinel or Log Analytics tables | Microsoft Defender XDR Advanced Hunting tables |
+| Queries that use `TimeGenerated` | Advanced Hunting queries that use `Timestamp` |
+| Response parsing from the existing query action's output | Response parsing from `schema` and `results` |
+
+The updated playbook flow is:
+
+1. Start from the existing Logic App trigger.
+2. Initialize or compose the Advanced Hunting query.
+3. Call Microsoft Graph by using `POST /security/runHuntingQuery`.
+4. Parse the response body.
+5. Loop over the `results` array.
+6. Run the existing enrichment, notification, or response actions.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+Before you update a Logic App playbook, make sure that the following requirements are met.
+
+| Requirement | Details |
+| --- | --- |
+| Microsoft Defender XDR access | Advanced Hunting data must be available in Microsoft Defender XDR. |
+| Logic App identity | Use a system-assigned managed identity, user-assigned managed identity, or application registration. |
+| Microsoft Graph permission | Grant `ThreatHunting.Read.All`. Admin consent is required. |
+| Query validation access | An administrator or analyst must be able to validate each query in Advanced Hunting in the Microsoft Defender portal. |
+| Change control | Test the changes in a nonproduction or cloned playbook before replacing production actions. |
+
+Before you update a production playbook, confirm table availability, permissions, and query behavior in your tenant.
+
+## Configure permissions and authentication
+
+The Advanced Hunting API requires the `ThreatHunting.Read.All` Microsoft Graph permission.
+
+| Permission type | Permission | Recommended use |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Application | `ThreatHunting.Read.All` | Recommended for production Logic App automation. |
+| Delegated | `ThreatHunting.Read.All` | Useful for user-context testing or interactive scenarios. |
+
+Use a managed identity where possible.
+
+If you use an HTTP action, configure it with the following settings:
+
+| Setting | Value |
+| --- | --- |
+| Authentication type | Managed Identity |
+| Identity | System-assigned or user-assigned managed identity |
+| Audience | `https://graph.microsoft.com` |
+| HTTP method | `POST` |
+| URI | `https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/runHuntingQuery` |
+
+If you use a Microsoft Graph connector or custom connector instead of the generic HTTP action, configure it to call the same endpoint with the required permissions and request body.
+
+## Call the Advanced Hunting API
+
+Use the following Microsoft Graph endpoint:
+
+```text
+POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/runHuntingQuery
+```
+
+The request uses the following headers:
+
+```text
+Content-Type: application/json
+Authorization: Bearer <token>
+```
+
+For example:
+
+```json
+{
+  "Query": "DeviceProcessEvents | where Timestamp > ago(1h) | take 100"
+}
+```
+
+You can also specify an explicit timespan:
+
+```json
+{
+  "Query": "DeviceProcessEvents | project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine",
+  "Timespan": "PT1H"
+}
+```
+
+The `Timespan` parameter is optional. You can also restrict the time range directly in the KQL query. If both are used, the narrower time range applies.
+
+## Update a Logic App playbook
+
+Update each playbook that runs queries against Log Analytics, Azure Monitor Logs, or workspace-based Microsoft Sentinel data.
+
+1. Identify every Logic App action that uses Log Analytics, Azure Monitor Logs, or workspace-based query execution.
+2. Copy the existing KQL query and identify which output columns are used by downstream actions.
+3. Map the Log Analytics tables and columns to their Advanced Hunting equivalents.
+
+    For table and schema changes, see [Update Microsoft Sentinel content to use Advanced Hunting tables](transition-advanced-hunting-tables).
+4. Replace `TimeGenerated` filters with `Timestamp`, where applicable.
+5. Validate the updated KQL query in Advanced Hunting in the Microsoft Defender portal.
+6. Replace the Log Analytics query action with a Microsoft Graph call to:
+
+    ```text
+    /security/runHuntingQuery
+    ```
+7. Update response parsing to use the `results` array.
+8. Update downstream expressions to use named JSON properties instead of row indexes, where applicable.
+9. Add handling for empty results and API errors.
+10. Test the playbook end to end before enabling the updated version in production.
+
+## Map commonly used tables
+
+The following table provides examples of Advanced Hunting tables commonly used by playbooks.
+
+| Data | Advanced Hunting table | Notes |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Defender XDR alert metadata | `AlertInfo` | Alert title, severity, category, service source, and alert ID |
+| Alert entities or evidence | `AlertEvidence` | Related users, devices, files, URLs, IP addresses, and evidence |
+| Device process activity | `DeviceProcessEvents` | Process creation and related endpoint process events |
+| Device network activity | `DeviceNetworkEvents` | Inbound and outbound network connection events |
+| Device file activity | `DeviceFileEvents` | File creation, modification, and file-system events |
+| Device registry activity | `DeviceRegistryEvents` | Registry creation, modification, and deletion events |
+| Device logon activity | `DeviceLogonEvents` | Device authentication and logon events |
+| Email events | `EmailEvents` | Email delivery and message metadata |
+| Email attachments | `EmailAttachmentInfo` | Attachment metadata for email messages |
+| Email URLs | `EmailUrlInfo` | URLs observed in email messages |
+| Post-delivery email actions | `EmailPostDeliveryEvents` | Post-delivery actions, such as zero-hour auto purge (ZAP) |
+| Cloud app activity | `CloudAppEvents` | Cloud application and SaaS activity |
+| Identity information | `IdentityInfo` or `IdentityAccountInfo` | Validate the table available in your tenant |
+| Microsoft Entra ID sign-in events | `EntraIdSignInEvents` or `AADSignInEventsBeta` | Use the table available in your Advanced Hunting schema |
+
+Table and column availability can vary based on licensing, tenant configuration, data-source onboarding, and schema changes. Validate the required tables in your tenant before updating a production playbook.
+
+## Update response parsing
+
+Log Analytics response formats depend on how the playbook runs the query. Azure Monitor Logs and Azure Log Analytics listing actions, including their deprecated versions, return a `value` array of objects with named fields. Direct Log Analytics query REST calls return `tables` and positional row arrays. Microsoft Graph Advanced Hunting returns `schema` and `results`.
+
+Change the loop input to `results`. Replace positional field references with named properties where used. If expressions already use named properties, update only those affected by changes to the query output.
+
+The following examples apply to playbooks that read `tables[0].rows`. They assume that the first two source columns map to `Timestamp` and `DeviceName`. Apply the same approach to every field the playbook uses.
+
+| Log Analytics pattern | Advanced Hunting pattern |
+| --- | --- |
+| `body('Run_query')?['tables'][0]?['rows']` | `body('Run_Hunting_Query')?['results']` |
+| `items('For_each')?[0]` | `items('For_each')?['Timestamp']` |
+| `items('For_each')?[1]` | `items('For_each')?['DeviceName']` |
+
+An Advanced Hunting response can look like the following example:
+
+```json
+{
+  "schema": [
+    {
+      "name": "Timestamp",
+      "type": "DateTime"
+    },
+    {
+      "name": "DeviceName",
+      "type": "String"
+    },
+    {
+      "name": "FileName",
+      "type": "String"
+    }
+  ],
+  "results": [
+    {
+      "Timestamp": "2026-06-23T08:00:00Z",
+      "DeviceName": "device01.contoso.com",
+      "FileName": "powershell.exe"
+    }
+  ]
+}
+```
+
+### Parse the response
+
+Add a **Parse JSON** action after the Microsoft Graph call.
+
+You can use the following schema as a starting point:
+
+```json
+{
+  "type": "object",
+  "properties": {
+    "schema": {
+      "type": "array",
+      "items": {
+        "type": "object",
+        "properties": {
+          "name": {
+            "type": "string"
+          },
+          "type": {
+            "type": "string"
+          }
+        }
+      }
+    },
+    "results": {
+      "type": "array",
+      "items": {
+        "type": "object"
+      }
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+Configure the **For each** action to iterate over:
+
+```text
+body('Parse_JSON')?['results']
+```
+
+## Update common playbook queries
+
+The following examples show how common Log Analytics queries can be updated to use Advanced Hunting.
+
+### Alert enrichment
+
+A Log Analytics query might use:
+
+```kusto
+SecurityAlert
+| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
+| where SystemAlertId == "<alert-id>"
+| project TimeGenerated, AlertName, ProviderName, AlertSeverity
+```
+
+Use the following Advanced Hunting query instead:
+
+```kusto
+AlertInfo
+| where Timestamp > ago(1h)
+| where AlertId == "<alert-id>"
+| project Timestamp, AlertId, Title, ServiceSource, Severity
+```
+
+The following fields change:
+
+| Log Analytics field | Advanced Hunting field |
+| --- | --- |
+| `TimeGenerated` | `Timestamp` |
+| `SystemAlertId` | `AlertId` |
+| `AlertName` | `Title` |
+| `ProviderName` | `ServiceSource` |
+| `AlertSeverity` | `Severity` |
+
+### Device process investigation
+
+For example:
+
+```json
+{
+  "Query": "DeviceProcessEvents | where Timestamp > ago(24h) | where DeviceName == '<device-name>' | project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine"
+}
+```
+
+### Email investigation
+
+For example:
+
+```kusto
+EmailEvents
+| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
+| where RecipientEmailAddress =~ "<user@contoso.com>"
+| project Timestamp, NetworkMessageId, SenderFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, DeliveryAction
+```
+
+## Handle empty results and errors
+
+A successful Advanced Hunting query can return no rows. Check the number of results before running downstream actions:
+
+```text
+length(body('Run_Hunting_Query')?['results'])
+```
+
+Continue only when the length is greater than `0`. Otherwise, end the flow gracefully or handle the no-results condition explicitly.
+
+Use the following guidance to troubleshoot common issues:
+
+| Issue | Likely cause | Recommended resolution |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `403 Forbidden` | Missing Microsoft Graph permission or admin consent | Grant `ThreatHunting.Read.All` and confirm admin consent. |
+| `401 Unauthorized` | Authentication configuration issue | Verify the managed identity, audience, and Microsoft Graph authentication configuration. |
+| Empty results | Table, field, time range, or data availability mismatch | Validate the query in Advanced Hunting and confirm that the expected data is available. |
+| Expression failure | The playbook still expects Log Analytics row arrays | Update expressions to use `results` and named JSON properties. |
+| Query timeout | The query is too broad or resource intensive | Add time filters, project fewer columns, reduce joins, and limit results. |
+| Field not found | The Advanced Hunting schema differs from Log Analytics | Review the Advanced Hunting schema and update the column names. |
+
+## Optimize query performance and reliability
+
+When you use Advanced Hunting queries in Logic App playbooks:
+
+- Include a time filter, such as `Timestamp > ago(1h)`.
+- Apply filters as early as possible.
+- Use `project` to return only the columns required by the playbook.
+- Avoid broad search operations across large datasets.
+- Use `take` or `limit` when the playbook doesn't require all matching rows.
+- Test query runtime in Advanced Hunting before using the query in automation.
+- Handle authentication, authorization, throttling, timeout, and empty-result scenarios.
+
+For example, prefer:
+
+```kusto
+DeviceProcessEvents
+| where Timestamp > ago(1h)
+| where DeviceName == "device01.contoso.com"
+| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
+| take 100
+```
+
+Avoid broad queries such as:
+
+```kusto
+DeviceProcessEvents
+| search "powershell"
+```
+
+## Validate the updated playbook
+
+Before you use the updated playbook in production, confirm that:
+
+- The Logic App no longer depends on the Log Analytics query action for the updated flow.
+- The playbook calls Microsoft Graph at `/security/runHuntingQuery`.
+- The Logic App identity has `ThreatHunting.Read.All` with admin consent.
+- The KQL query works as expected in Advanced Hunting.
+- Log Analytics tables and columns are mapped to the appropriate Advanced Hunting equivalents.
+- Response parsing uses `results`.
+- Downstream actions reference named properties instead of row indexes.
+- Empty-result handling is configured.
+- Error handling is configured for authentication, authorization, throttling, and timeout scenarios.
+- The playbook has been tested end to end with a controlled test case.
+
+## API limits and operational considerations
+
+Microsoft Graph Advanced Hunting queries can return up to 100,000 rows per request. The optional `Timespan` parameter defaults to 30 days.
+
+The API is also subject to tenant-level quotas and resource allocation. A `429` response indicates throttling or resource pressure. Retry the request later and review the response for more information.
+
+Long-running requests can time out. Optimize the KQL query and narrow the time range when needed.
+
+Explicitly define the time scope used by automation, either in KQL or through the request timespan.
\ No newline at end of file

+# Transition MSSP-managed deployments to Microsoft Defender | Microsoft Learn
+
+Managed security service providers (MSSPs) often manage detections, workbooks, automation, and access across multiple customer tenants.
+
+When transitioning existing Microsoft Sentinel deployments to Integrated Security Operations Center (ISOC) in Microsoft Defender, MSSPs must update their content deployment processes and validate access to ensure that security operations continue to function across customer environments.
+
+This article describes the operational considerations and validation steps for transitioning MSSP-managed deployments.
+
+Note
+
+ISOC is in preview. Capabilities and availability might change during the preview period.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+Before transitioning MSSP-managed deployments:
+
+- Ensure that each customer tenant is [eligible for ISOC](/en-us/defender-xdr/isoc-overview).
+- Identify existing Microsoft Sentinel analytics rules, workbooks, automation, and other content managed by the MSSP.
+- Identify the content distribution profiles, CI/CD pipelines, and deployment definitions used across customer tenants.
+- Verify that the MSSP has the required delegated access and permissions in each customer tenant.
+- Identify any content managed jointly by the MSSP and the customer.
+- If you use [Tenant Governance (GDAP)](/en-us/defender-xdr/governance-relationships), ensure that you've adopted Unified RBAC.
+
+## Update content deployment processes
+
+Review and update the processes used to deploy and manage content across customer tenants.
+
+### Update content distribution profiles
+
+Update content distribution profiles to deploy content that uses Microsoft Defender Advanced Hunting instead of Microsoft Sentinel workspace-based content.
+
+Ensure that the updated profiles deploy:
+
+- Custom detections instead of Microsoft Sentinel analytics rules.
+- Workbooks that use Advanced Hunting data sources.
+- Updated automation and Logic App playbooks.
+
+For more information, see:
+
+- [Convert analytics rules to custom detections](transition-custom-detections)
+- [Update workbooks to use Advanced Hunting data](update-workbooks-advanced-hunting-data)
+- [Update Logic App playbook automation](transition-logic-app-playbooks)
+
+### Update CI/CD pipelines and deployment definitions
+
+If you use CI/CD pipelines or infrastructure as code to deploy content across customer tenants, update the repositories, deployment pipelines, and automation processes.
+
+Ensure that deployment definitions use the converted detections and Advanced Hunting-based content model consistently across customer tenants.
+
+Validate that the updated deployment processes deploy the expected content before reducing ingestion into Microsoft Sentinel.
+
+## Validate delegated access and permissions
+
+MSSPs must have the required delegated access and permissions in each customer tenant to manage and validate the transitioned content.
+
+Before beginning migration activities:
+
+1. Review the delegated access configured for each customer tenant.
+
+    Note
+
+    If you use Tenant Governance (GDAP) and assign permissions through ARM, migrate to Unified RBAC.
+2. Verify that the MSSP has the required permissions for the Defender workloads and data used by the transitioned content.
+3. Review user and group access to identify any permissions that must be updated.
+4. Use SOC Optimization recommendations to identify potential access gaps.
+5. Resolve identified access gaps and confirm that analysts can access the required data after the transition.
+
+For more information about updating permissions, see [Update permissions and roles with Unified RBAC](transition-unified-rbac).
+
+Important
+
+Unified RBAC is mandatory when you enable ISOC. MDE device groups aren't currently supported with Tenant Governance (GDAP).
+
+## Define shared content ownership
+
+In some customer environments, both the MSSP and the customer manage detections, workbooks, or automation.
+
+Before transitioning these environments, establish ownership and change-control processes to avoid conflicting updates.
+
+Review the following considerations:
+
+- **Content ownership**: Identify whether the MSSP or customer is responsible for managing each detection, workbook, and automation resource.
+- **Change control**: Establish how changes to shared content are reviewed and applied.
+- **Deployment responsibilities**: Determine who is responsible for updating and validating content deployments.
+- **Ongoing management**: Confirm how the MSSP and customer coordinate changes after the transition.
+
+## Validate MSSP-managed deployments
+
+Before reducing data ingestion into Microsoft Sentinel for a customer tenant, verify that the transitioned content and access configurations work as expected.
+
+Complete the following validation steps for each customer tenant:
+
+1. **Validate content distribution profiles.**
+
+    Confirm that content distribution profiles deploy the converted custom detections, Advanced Hunting-based workbooks, and updated automation.
+2. **Validate CI/CD pipelines and deployment definitions.**
+
+    Confirm that repositories, pipelines, and deployment definitions have been updated to deploy content that uses the Advanced Hunting data model.
+3. **Validate delegated access and permissions.**
+
+    Verify that the MSSP has the required delegated access and Defender workload permissions in the customer tenant.
+4. **Validate shared content ownership.**
+
+    Confirm that ownership and change-control responsibilities are defined for content managed jointly by the MSSP and customer.
+5. **Validate user and group access.**
+
+    Confirm that access reviews are complete, identified gaps are resolved, and analysts retain access to the data required for security operations.
+
+Important
+
+Complete the applicable content migration and validation steps before reducing ingestion into Microsoft Sentinel. Ensure that all resources dependent on a table have been updated to use the corresponding Advanced Hunting data and validated.
\ No newline at end of file

+# Optimize Microsoft Defender XDR data ingestion | Microsoft Learn
+
+When Microsoft Defender XDR data is available directly in Advanced Hunting, you can update Microsoft Sentinel content to use the corresponding Advanced Hunting tables and then stop duplicate ingestion of that data into Microsoft Sentinel.
+
+Update your content one table at a time. When the content for all tables is updated and validated, stop ingestion for the supported Microsoft Defender XDR tables in the workspace at the same time.
+
+Important
+
+You can't stop ingestion for a single table. **Configure workspace** stops ingesting data into Log Analytics for the supported Defender XDR tables in the workspace at the same time, except tables with analytics retention set to 180 days or more, which stay ingested. Don't select it until you've updated and validated all content that depends on any of these tables. Otherwise, detections, workbooks, queries, and automation can stop receiving the data they require.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+Before you begin, make sure that:
+
+- Your tenant is [eligible for ISOC](/en-us/defender-xdr/isoc-overview).
+- You have an existing Microsoft Sentinel workspace that ingests Microsoft Defender XDR data that is also available through Advanced Hunting.
+- You have access to the [Microsoft Defender portal](https://security.microsoft.com) and Advanced Hunting.
+- You have permissions to review and update the Microsoft Sentinel and Microsoft Defender content that depends on the tables you're optimizing.
+- You have identified the queries, analytics rules, workbooks, Logic App playbooks, reports, and other content that depend on each table you plan to transition.
+
+For information about updating access when moving from workspace-based data to Microsoft Defender XDR data, see [Update permissions and roles with Unified RBAC](transition-unified-rbac).
+
+## Prepare dependent content
+
+Before you stop ingestion, update content that currently queries the Microsoft Sentinel table so that it can use the corresponding Advanced Hunting data.
+
+Use the following sequence:
+
+| Area | Action |
+| --- | --- |
+| Queries and other KQL content | Update queries to use the corresponding Advanced Hunting tables and schema. |
+| Permissions and roles | Make sure users and automation identities have access to the required Microsoft Defender workloads. |
+| Analytics rules | Recreate applicable Microsoft Sentinel analytics rules as Microsoft Defender custom detections. |
+| Workbooks | Update workbook queries to use the Advanced Hunting data source. |
+| Logic App playbooks | Replace Log Analytics query actions with queries to the Microsoft Graph Advanced Hunting API where applicable. |
+| Ingestion | Stop ingestion for the supported Defender XDR tables only after the content for all tables is updated and validated. |
+
+For detailed migration guidance, see:
+
+- [Update Microsoft Sentinel content to use Advanced Hunting tables](transition-advanced-hunting-tables)
+- [Update permissions and roles with Unified RBAC](transition-unified-rbac)
+- [Convert Microsoft Sentinel analytics rules to custom detections](transition-custom-detections)
+- [Update workbooks to use Advanced Hunting data](update-workbooks-advanced-hunting-data)
+- [Update Logic App playbook automation to use Advanced Hunting](transition-logic-app-playbooks)
+
+## Validate content before you stop ingestion
+
+For each table, validate all dependent content before you stop ingestion.
+
+Make sure that:
+
+- **Detections**: Every analytics rule that queries the table has an equivalent custom detection running against Advanced Hunting data.
+- **Workbooks**: Every workbook that uses the table has been updated to use the Advanced Hunting data source and renders correctly for its intended users.
+- **Automation**: Every Logic App playbook that queries the table has been updated to use the Microsoft Graph Advanced Hunting API where required and has passed an end-to-end test.
+- **Access**: Users, groups, and automation identities that require the data have access to the corresponding Microsoft Defender workload.
+- **Queries and reports**: Queries, saved hunts, scheduled reports, and other content that previously referenced the Microsoft Sentinel table return the expected results against Advanced Hunting.
+- **Deployment**: If you use CI/CD or repeatable deployment definitions, make sure they deploy the updated custom detections and Advanced Hunting-based content.
+
+Validate dependencies before you stop ingestion. In particular, validate detections, workbooks, automation, and access for every table.
+
+## Stop ingestion for the supported Defender XDR tables
+
+If you use data collection rules (DCRs) on these tables, check them first. To keep a DCR working on a table, set that table's retention to 180 days or more before you select **Configure workspace**. For more information, see [Check data collection rules and transformations before you stop ingestion](transition-soc-optimization-recommendations#dcr-xdr-tables).
+
+After you complete all **Lower Defender data costs** recommendations and validate all dependent content:
+
+1. In the Microsoft Defender portal, go to **Setup & configuration** > **Data management** > **Data & connectors**.
+2. Select the **Tables** tab.
+3. Select **Configure workspace**.
+
+This stops ingesting Defender XDR data into Log Analytics for the supported Defender XDR tables in the workspace. This is what lowers your costs.
+
+## Validate after you stop ingestion
+
+After you stop ingestion, confirm that ingestion changed as expected and that your security operations content continues to work.
+
+Monitor the updated configuration over several detection and automation runs.
+
+Verify that:
+
+- Custom detections continue to return the expected results from Advanced Hunting data.
+- Hunting queries and other KQL content return the expected results.
+- Workbook tiles render correctly for their intended users.
+- Logic App playbooks continue to trigger and complete successfully.
+- Users and automation identities retain access to the required data.
+
+If content doesn't behave as expected, review its Advanced Hunting table mapping, schema, permissions, and query configuration.
+
+## Update content table by table
+
+You don't need to update the content for every Microsoft Defender XDR table at the same time. For each table:
+
+1. Identify the content that depends on the table.
+2. Update the dependent content to use Advanced Hunting.
+3. Validate queries, detections, workbooks, automation, and access.
+4. Set the recommendation status to **Completed**.
+5. Continue with the next table.
+
+After all tables are complete, stop ingestion for the supported Defender XDR tables.
