+# Review Microsoft Sentinel recommendations for ISOC (Preview) | Microsoft Learn
+
+When you transition an existing Microsoft Sentinel deployment to Integrated Security Operations Center (ISOC), you can use supported Microsoft Defender XDR data directly in the Microsoft Defender portal instead of relying on the same data being ingested into Microsoft Sentinel.
+
+SOC optimization recommendations help you identify Microsoft Defender XDR data to review and the Microsoft Sentinel content that might need to be updated before ingestion changes.
+
+Use the preview migration tool in a recommendation to convert eligible analytics rules to custom detections. Validate them while the original rules remain enabled, and complete migration when you're ready.
+
+Note
+
+The migration tool and the migration, validation, completion, and alert compatibility behavior documented here are in **PREVIEW**. See the [Supplemental Terms of Use for Microsoft Azure Previews](https://azure.microsoft.com/support/legal/preview-supplemental-terms/) for additional legal terms that apply to Azure features that are in beta, preview, or otherwise not yet released into general availability.
+
+Important
+
+Update and validate dependent content table by table, including queries, detections, permissions, workbooks, automation, and data collection rules (DCRs). You can't stop ingestion for a single table. After all tables are done, **Configure workspace** stops ingestion for the supported Defender XDR tables in the workspace at the same time, except tables with analytics retention set to 180 days or more, which stay ingested. If ingestion stops before content is updated, existing content can stop receiving data, which creates coverage gaps.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+Before you review SOC optimization recommendations:
+
+- Connect all Microsoft Sentinel workspaces in your deployment to the Microsoft Defender portal. For more information, see [Transition an existing Microsoft Sentinel deployment to ISOC](transition-existing-sentinel-deployment).
+- Make sure you have access to SOC optimization and the permissions required to review and update the Microsoft Sentinel and Microsoft Defender content in your environment.
+- Review the [ISOC eligibility and workspace requirements](/en-us/defender-xdr/isoc-overview).
+
+Before you use the preview migration tool:
+
+- Confirm that you can migrate analytics rules, manage custom detections, and update dependent automation. Review [Microsoft Sentinel roles and permissions](roles) and [permissions for managing custom detections](/en-us/defender-xdr/custom-detection-rules#required-permissions-for-managing-custom-detections).
+- Plan how to compare alerts, entities, severity, scheduling, and downstream automation during validation.
+- During preview, configure an alert tuning rule to automatically resolve alerts associated with custom detections under validation. Both the original analytics rule and the custom detection generate alerts during this stage.
+- During preview, re-create applicable health monitors as custom detection rules so that you can validate them during migration.
+
+SOC optimization recommendations can take up to 48 hours to appear after workspace onboarding or changes to table retention.
+
+For more information about SOC optimization, see [Optimize your security operations](soc-optimization/soc-optimization-access).
+
+## Review SOC optimization recommendations
+
+Review SOC optimization recommendations to identify Microsoft Defender XDR tables that might be affected by changes to Microsoft Sentinel ingestion.
+
+1. [Sign in to the Microsoft Defender portal](https://security.microsoft.com/).
+2. In the left menu, select **SOC optimization**.
+3. Review the **Lower Defender data costs** recommendations. Each recommendation covers one table in one workspace.
+4. Note the table and the workspace for each recommendation.
+5. For each table, identify all content and integrations that depend on the corresponding Microsoft Sentinel data.
+
+The recommendation details pane and the **Update your content to use Defender data** side panel include a **Before stopping ingestion** section. It explains how data collection rules (DCRs) and user and entity behavior analytics (UEBA) are affected when you stop ingestion. For what this means and what to do, see Check data collection rules and transformations before you stop ingestion.
+
+Don't stop ingestion until you've reviewed and validated the dependencies for all affected tables.
+
+## Track your progress
+
+The **SOC optimization** page shows this banner: **Lower Defender data costs: Review the SOC optimization recommendations and update your content to lower your costs.**
+
+![Screenshot of the Lower Defender data costs banner on the SOC optimization page, with the See what you need to do button.](media/transition-soc-optimization-recommendations/soc-optimization-banner.png)
+
+To see what to do and track your progress, select **See what you need to do** on the banner. After you start working on recommendations, the button changes to **View progress**. The **Lower Defender data costs** section header on the page has the same link. It also shows **View all** when there are more recommendations than fit in one row.
+
+The **Update your content to use Defender data** side panel opens. The panel shows:
+
+- **Content counts**: the number of analytics rules, workbooks, and playbooks that use the tables.
+- **Lower Defender data costs recommendations**: a progress bar for **Resolved recommendations** (for example, 3/10), and the number of recommendations in each status: **Not started**, **In progress**, **Completed**, and **Dismissed**.
+- **What you gain**: the value of moving your content to Defender data.
+- **What to do**: the steps to follow. These match the steps in Work through Lower Defender data costs recommendations.
+- **Before stopping ingestion**: how data collection rules (DCRs) and UEBA are affected when you stop ingestion.
+- **Required permissions**: the roles you need.
+- A note that only tables with 90 days of retention or less are included.
+
+[![Screenshot of the Update your content to use Defender data side panel, showing content counts and recommendation progress.](media/transition-soc-optimization-recommendations/soc-optimization-progress-panel.png)](media/transition-soc-optimization-recommendations/soc-optimization-progress-panel.png#lightbox)
+
+A recommendation is resolved when its status is set to **Completed** or **Dismissed**. When all **Lower Defender data costs** recommendations are **Completed** or **Dismissed**, the banner and the section header link no longer appear. After you've updated and validated all dependent content, stop ingestion as described in Work through Lower Defender data costs recommendations.
+
+## Review a Lower Defender data costs recommendation
+
+Each recommendation covers one table in one workspace. Select a recommendation to open its details pane. The pane includes these sections:
+
+| Section | What it shows |
+| --- | --- |
+| **Why we recommend this** | Why SOC optimization recommends this change for the table. |
+| **Monthly estimated data volume** | The estimated monthly data volume for the table. |
+| **What we've found** | The number of analytics rules, workbooks, and playbooks that use the table. |
+| **What to do** | The steps to update your content. |
+| **Before stopping ingestion** | How data collection rules (DCRs) and, for some tables, UEBA are affected when you stop ingestion. |
+| **Table details** | Details about the table. The pane shows: "Data is calculated and refreshed every 24 hours." |
+
+In the pane, you can select **Change status**, **Provide feedback**, or **View full details**.
+
+[![Screenshot of a Lower Defender data costs recommendation details pane with Why we recommend this, What we've found, and What to do sections.](media/transition-soc-optimization-recommendations/soc-optimization-recommendation-pane.png)](media/transition-soc-optimization-recommendations/soc-optimization-recommendation-pane.png#lightbox)
+
+Select **View full details** to open the recommendation page. The **Analytic rules**, **Playbooks**, and **Workbooks** tabs list the content that uses the table. To migrate analytics rules, use the **Analytic rules** tab. For more information, see Migrate analytics rules with the migration tool.
+
+[![Screenshot of a Lower Defender data costs recommendation page with the Analytic rules, Playbooks, and Workbooks tabs.](media/transition-soc-optimization-recommendations/soc-optimization-recommendation-page.png)](media/transition-soc-optimization-recommendations/soc-optimization-recommendation-page.png#lightbox)
+
+Note
+
+- The **Analytic rules**, **Playbooks**, and **Workbooks** tabs list content that queried the table in the last 90 days. The lists refresh every 24 hours, so recent changes might not show yet, and deleted content might still be listed. A list can also include content that uses the table through a parser or function, or that only mentions the table in a comment. For analytics rules, this includes detections that use Advanced Security Information Model (ASIM) normalization. Review each item before you change it.
+- The list shows only analytics rules, workbooks, and playbooks. If it's empty, still check for other content that uses the table, such as hunting queries, summary rules, DCRs, and external tools, before you set the status to **Completed**.
+
+## Work through Lower Defender data costs recommendations
+
+Do steps 1–5 for each recommendation. Do step 6 once, after all recommendations are complete.
+
+1. Update Defender role-based access control (RBAC). Make sure that the users, groups, and automation identities that use the data have the required permissions in Microsoft Defender. For more information, see Update permissions and roles.
+2. Open each **Lower Defender data costs** recommendation, and review the content that uses the table.
+3. Update the content to query Defender data with Advanced Hunting. To migrate analytics rules, see Migrate analytics rules with the migration tool. For other content, see Update dependent content.
+4. Test the updated content. For more information, see Validate your updated content.
+5. Set the status of the recommendation manually. When you start, select **Change status** > **In progress**. When you finish, set the status to **Completed**. If you don't plan to act on the recommendation, set the status to **Dismissed**.
+6. After you complete all **Lower Defender data costs** recommendations, stop ingesting Defender XDR data into Log Analytics for the supported Defender XDR tables in the workspace. In the Defender portal, go to **Setup & configuration** > **Data management** > **Data & connectors**, select the **Tables** tab, and then select **Configure workspace**. Stopping this ingestion lowers your costs.
+
+Note
+
+- **Lower Defender data costs** recommendations don't complete automatically. Set the status yourself.
+- Completing a rule migration sets the rule status to **Completed**. It doesn't change the status of the recommendation.
+
+## Identify dependent content
+
+For each table that you plan to transition, identify all content that queries, processes, or depends on that data.
+
+Review dependencies including:
+
+- Hunting and saved queries.
+- Analytics rules.
+- Custom detections.
+- Workbooks.
+- Logic App playbooks.
+- Continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) deployments and repositories.
+- Reports and API integrations.
+- User, group, and automation permissions.
+- Data collection rules (DCRs) and transformations on the table, including filter and split rules from the **Tables** page.
+
+Search your queries and content repositories for references to the affected Microsoft Sentinel tables so that you can identify dependencies that aren't surfaced directly by a SOC optimization recommendation.
+
+## Update dependent content
+
+The changes required depend on how each table is used in your environment.
+
+| Area | What to review and update |
+| --- | --- |
+| Queries and content | Update Kusto Query Language (KQL) queries to use the corresponding Advanced Hunting tables and schemas. |
+| Permissions and roles | Make sure users and groups have access to the corresponding Microsoft Defender workloads through Microsoft Defender unified role-based access control (RBAC). |
+| Analytics rules | Convert applicable Microsoft Sentinel analytics rules to Microsoft Defender custom detections and validate detection behavior. |
+| Workbooks | Update workbook queries to use Advanced Hunting data and validate tiles, filters, and parameters. |
+| Logic App playbooks | Replace Log Analytics or Azure Monitor Logs query actions with Microsoft Graph Advanced Hunting API calls where required. |
+| CI/CD | Review deployed content and repositories for references to Microsoft Sentinel tables or other workspace-specific dependencies. |
+| DCRs and transformations | Keep the table at 180 days or more to keep the DCR working, or move its logic into queries in Defender. See Check data collection rules and transformations. |
+| Ingestion | Change ingestion only after all affected content has been updated and validated. |
+
+### Update queries to use Advanced Hunting tables
+
+Update queries that use Microsoft Sentinel workspace tables so that they use the corresponding Microsoft Defender XDR Advanced Hunting tables.
+
+Depending on the table, changes can include:
+
+- Replacing Microsoft Sentinel table names with their Advanced Hunting equivalents.
+- Keeping or replacing `TimeGenerated`. When your Microsoft Sentinel workspace is connected to the Defender portal, `TimeGenerated` works in Advanced Hunting. For new queries, and for custom detections that run in near real time (**Continuous (NRT)** frequency), use `Timestamp`. `CallActivityEvents` doesn't have a `Timestamp` column. For that table, use `ActivityTimestamp`. For more information, see [Changes that apply to all tables](transition-advanced-hunting-tables#changes-that-apply-to-all-tables).
+- Updating field names and data types.
+- Removing dependencies on Sentinel-specific metadata fields that aren't available in Advanced Hunting.
+
+Validate each updated query in Advanced Hunting before using it in production content.
+
+For more information, see [Update content to use Advanced Hunting tables](transition-advanced-hunting-tables).
+
+### Update permissions and roles
+
+Access to Microsoft Sentinel workspace data doesn't automatically provide access to the corresponding Microsoft Defender workload data.
+
+Make sure affected users and groups have the required Microsoft Defender permissions before changing ingestion.
+
+For more information, see [Update permissions and roles with Unified RBAC](transition-unified-rbac).
+
+### Update analytics rules and custom detections
+
+Review Microsoft Sentinel analytics rules that depend on affected tables.
+
+For eligible rules, use the preview migration tool. Validate differences in scheduling, entity mappings, alert configuration, automation, and other rule behavior before completing migration.
+
+For rules that the tool can't convert, see [Manually convert analytics rules to custom detections](transition-custom-detections).
+
+### Update workbooks
+
+Review workbook queries that depend on affected Microsoft Sentinel tables.
+
+Update applicable workbook queries to use Advanced Hunting data, and validate:
+
+- Queries.
+- Tiles and visualizations.
+- Filters.
+- Parameters.
+- User access to the underlying data.
+
+For more information, see [Update workbooks to use Advanced Hunting data](update-workbooks-advanced-hunting-data).
+
+### Update Logic App playbooks
+
+Review Logic App playbooks that query Log Analytics, Azure Monitor Logs, or workspace-based Microsoft Sentinel data.
+
+Where required, update the playbook to use the Microsoft Graph Advanced Hunting API and validate authentication, query results, response parsing, and downstream actions.
+
+For more information, see [Update Logic App playbook automation](transition-logic-app-playbooks).
+
+### Review CI/CD deployments
+
+Review CI/CD repositories and deployments for content that references affected Microsoft Sentinel tables or workspace-specific resources.
+
+Update and validate affected deployments before changing ingestion.
+
+For more information, see [Deploy content as code with CI/CD in ISOC](/en-us/defender-xdr/deploy-content-integrated-security-operations).
+
+## Migrate analytics rules with the migration tool (Preview)
+
+Use the preview migration tool to migrate one rule or all eligible rules in a recommendation. Each rule moves through migration, validation, and completion independently.
+
+Important
+
+The original analytics rule remains enabled while the custom detection is created and validated. Only **Complete migration** disables the original rule. Don't stop ingestion until you've validated all dependent content for all Defender XDR tables.
+
+### Review rule eligibility
+
+Open the recommendation for the table that you plan to transition and check each rule's status.
+
+1. In the [Microsoft Defender portal](https://security.microsoft.com/), open **SOC optimization**.
+2. Select the **Lower Defender data costs** recommendation for the affected table.
+3. Select the **Analytic rules** tab and review the migration summary and per-rule statuses.
+
+    [![Screenshot of the preview migration status summary and analytics rules with Ready to migrate and Migration unavailable statuses.](media/transition-soc-optimization-recommendations/migration-rule-statuses.png)](media/transition-soc-optimization-recommendations/migration-rule-statuses.png#lightbox)
+4. For a rule marked **Migration unavailable**, select **Open migration tool**, and on the **Get started** tab select **Download CSV** to review the blocker. Modify the rule where appropriate or follow the [manual conversion guidance](transition-custom-detections). Keep the original rule enabled until you've validated its replacement.
+
+Eligibility and migration are separate. Being listed in a recommendation doesn't mean a rule is ready to migrate.
+
+| Status | Meaning | Next action |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| **Ready to migrate** | The rule is eligible for conversion by the migration tool. | Start migration for the rule. |
+| **Migration unavailable** | The current migration flow can't convert the rule. | Download the CSV report and review the reason. |
+| **Validation required** | The custom detection was created and generates tagged alerts while the original analytics rule remains enabled. | Compare behavior and dependent automation before completing migration. |
+| **Completed** | The custom detection is enabled and editable, and the original analytics rule is disabled. | Confirm the final state and review other dependencies. |
+
+### Start migration
+
+Choose the scope carefully. Starting migration creates custom detections for validation; it doesn't disable the original analytics rules.
+
+To migrate one rule:
+
+1. On the **Analytic rules** tab, select a rule marked **Ready to migrate** to open its side panel.
+2. Select **Migrate rule**.
+3. Wait for the migration to finish. The rule then shows **Validation required**.
+
+To migrate all eligible rules in the recommendation:
+
+1. Select **Open migration tool**.
+2. On the **Get started** tab, review the **Migration**, **Validation**, and **Completion** stages.
+3. Select **Migrate now**.
+
+    Important
+
+    **Migrate now** starts migration for all rules marked **Ready to migrate** in the recommendation. Filtering the recommendation's rule list doesn't narrow the migration scope. Rules for which migration isn't available aren't included.
+
+Rules are processed independently. In a bulk migration, a rule that fails or remains unavailable doesn't prevent successfully created rules from moving to validation.
+
+### Validate the custom detections
+
+During preview validation, both the custom detection and its original analytics rule generate alerts. The custom detection's alerts are tagged for validation. Use the alert tuning rule you configured to reduce duplicate alert noise; don't assume those alerts are automatically resolved without it.
+
+1. Open the migration tool and select **Rules being validated**. On the **Detection rules** page, you can also select **Review rules under validation** to filter the list to rules in validation.
+2. Review each custom detection over a representative period.
+3. Compare alert volume, timing, severity, title, entities, and scheduling with the original analytics rule.
+4. Verify that downstream automation works with the custom detection's alerts. Review the preview alert compatibility differences when comparing results.
+
+    [![Screenshot of the preview migration validation panel with Complete migration and Cancel and delete actions.](media/transition-soc-optimization-recommendations/migration-validation-panel.png)](media/transition-soc-optimization-recommendations/migration-validation-panel.png#lightbox)
+
+During validation, you can edit migrated custom detections, except the alert title. If a rule needs more validation, leave it in validation. You don't have to complete every rule in a bulk migration at the same time.
+
+### Complete or cancel migration
+
+Complete migration only for rules whose detection results and dependent automation you've validated. Completion is the point at which the original analytics rule is disabled.
+
+Important
+
+In the preview migration flow, the disabled original analytics rule is automatically deleted after 90 days. Validate the replacement and its dependent automation before completing migration.
+
+1. In the validation panel, select the rules that passed validation.
+2. Select **Complete migration**. The custom detections are enabled and editable, and the corresponding analytics rules are disabled. You can also complete migration from the custom detection page.
+3. Return to the recommendation and confirm that those rules show **Completed**.
+
+    [![Screenshot of preview rule statuses showing one rule with Migration unavailable and two completed migrations.](media/transition-soc-optimization-recommendations/migration-completed-rules.png)](media/transition-soc-optimization-recommendations/migration-completed-rules.png#lightbox)
+4. Update and validate all remaining rules and other dependencies for the table. Then set the recommendation status to **Completed**. Recommendations don't complete automatically.
+
+To abandon a migration before completion, select the rule in the validation panel and choose **Cancel and delete**. The new custom detection is deleted, and the original analytics rule remains enabled.
+
+### Review alert compatibility differences (Preview)
+
+Alerts from migrated custom detections preserve selected analytics-rule properties to support existing Microsoft Sentinel flows. They don't have exactly the same properties as alerts from other custom detections. Validate your integrations rather than assuming every existing flow is compatible.
+
+The following values describe the **Microsoft Sentinel view** of alerts in workspaces onboarded to the Defender portal. Optional properties depend on the information available for each alert.
+
+| Property | Value for a migrated rule in Microsoft Sentinel | Validation consideration |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `ProviderName` | `Microsoft Sentinel` | Other custom detections use `MicrosoftThreatProtection` or `MDATP`. |
+| `ProductComponentName` | `ASI Scheduled Alerts` or `ASI NRT Alerts` | Identifies the rule type. |
+| `ProductName` | `Azure Sentinel` | The migrated rule's product name is also `Azure Sentinel` in Defender. |
+| `AlertType` | `<sourceWorkspaceId>_<sourceAnalyticRuleId>` | Defender keeps the custom detection detector ID instead of this Sentinel compatibility value. |
+| `ExtendedProperties["Analytic Rule Ids"]` | Same value as in the source analytics rule. | Identifies the original analytics rule, not the custom detection. |
+| `ExtendedProperties["Analytic Rule Name"]` | Same value as in the source analytics rule. | Separate from the generated alert title. |
+| `ExtendedProperties["MigratedAnalyticRule"]` | `"true"` | Identifies alerts from migrated rules. |
+| `ExtendedProperties["Correlation Id"]` | The rule execution ID. | Identifies an execution, not an individual alert. |
+| `ExtendedProperties["Query Start Time UTC"]` and `ExtendedProperties["Query End Time UTC"]` | Same values as in the source analytics rule. | Different from the alert's activity start and end times. |
+| `ExtendedProperties["Query Period"]` | Same value as in the source analytics rule. | Review integrations that use the query period. |
+| `ExtendedProperties["Trigger Operator"]` and `ExtendedProperties["Trigger Threshold"]` | Same values as in the source analytics rule. | Review integrations that use the trigger configuration. |
+| `ExtendedProperties["Event Grouping"]` | Same value as in the source analytics rule. | Describes alert generation, not incident grouping. |
+| `ExtendedProperties["Search Query Results Overall Count"]` | Same value as in the source analytics rule, when available. | Don't assume a total result count is available for grouped alerts. |
+| `ExtendedProperties["Data Sources"]` | Same value as in the source analytics rule. | Review integrations that use data-source metadata. |
+| `ExtendedProperties["Query"]` and `ExtendedProperties["OriginalQuery"]` | Not available in this preview. | Integrations that depend on these fields need review before completion. |
+
+### Review known issues and troubleshoot migration (Preview)
+
+Review these preview limitations before completing migration:
+
+- For rules configured to group all events into one alert, two duplicate alerts can occasionally reach the `SecurityAlert` table and downstream automation instead of one.
+- `ExtendedProperties["Query"]` and `ExtendedProperties["OriginalQuery"]` aren't available on alerts from migrated custom detections.
+
+Use the per-rule status and surfaced errors to decide what to do next.
+
+| Symptom | Action |
+| --- | --- |
+| **Migrate now** is unavailable. | No rules are marked **Ready to migrate**. If evaluation hasn't finished, wait and select **Refresh**. |
+| A rule shows **Migration unavailable**. | Download the CSV report, review the per-rule reason, and use the manual conversion guidance where needed. |
+| Validation needs more time or exposes a problem. | Leave the rule in validation, or use **Cancel and delete** before completion. The original analytics rule remains enabled. |
+
+## Validate your updated content
+
+Before you stop ingestion, validate the affected content end to end.
+
+Make sure that:
+
+- Updated KQL queries return the expected data in Advanced Hunting.
+- Analysts and other users can access the required Microsoft Defender data.
+- Custom detections generate the expected alerts.
+- Workbooks return the expected results.
+- Logic App playbooks run successfully with the updated data source.
+- CI/CD deployments don't reintroduce outdated table references or configurations.
+- Reports, APIs, and other integrations continue to return the expected data.
+- You've reviewed any DCR or transformation on the table and chosen an option for it.
+
+Complete validation for one table before continuing to the next table.
+
+## Check data collection rules and transformations before you stop ingestion
+
+Some organizations use a [data collection rule (DCR)](/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/data-collection/data-collection-rule-overview) to change Microsoft Defender XDR data before it's stored in their Microsoft Sentinel workspace. For example, they filter rows, send part of the data to the data lake, hide fields, or add new fields. This is also called a [workspace transformation, or a workspace transformation DCR](/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/data-collection/data-collection-transformations). [Filter and split rules](transformation-filter-split) that you create on the **Tables** page in the Defender portal also use a DCR.
+
+This section applies to you if a DCR changes a Microsoft Defender XDR table (XDR table). Most of it matters when you stop ingestion with **Configure workspace**. The user and entity behavior analytics (UEBA) part applies if UEBA uses the DeviceLogonEvents table. If you don't use DCRs on XDR tables, you can skip this section.
+
+### What happens when you stop ingestion
+
+A DCR runs only on data that's ingested into your Microsoft Sentinel workspace. When you select **Configure workspace** on the **Tables** tab of **Data & connectors**, Defender XDR tables are no longer ingested into the workspace, so the DCR no longer applies to them. Tables with analytics retention set to 180 days or more stay ingested, and their DCR keeps working. The original, unchanged data stays available in Defender for 90 days, and you can query it in [Advanced Hunting](/en-us/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-overview).
+
+You might already see unfiltered data in Advanced Hunting today. [Filter and split rules on XDR tables don't show in Advanced Hunting for the first 30 days of data](transformation-filter-split#known-limitations).
+
+The following table describes the effect for common DCR uses:
+
+| What you use the DCR for | What changes when you stop ingestion | What you can do |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Filter rows or remove columns to lower cost | The filter no longer applies. Microsoft Sentinel charges for ingesting this table stop. | No action needed for cost. Queries and rules that you move to Defender see the unfiltered data, so check their results. |
+| Send part of the data to the data lake only ([split rule](transformation-filter-split) on the Tables page) | The `_SPLT` table and the data lake copy of this table stop receiving new data, because the [data lake mirrors the data that's ingested into the workspace](manage-data-overview). Defender keeps the data for 90 days. | If you need the data for longer than 90 days, keep the table at 180 days or more, or use [streaming export from Defender](/en-us/defender-xdr/streaming-api) to your own storage. |
+| Add or calculate fields ([columns that end in `_CF`](/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/tutorial-workspace-transformations-portal)) | These fields don't exist in the Defender table. Queries and rules that use them fail. | [Calculate the field in the query](transition-advanced-hunting-tables), or keep the table at 180 days or more. |
+| Copy data to a custom table | The custom table stops receiving new data. | Keep the table at 180 days or more, or use [streaming export from Defender](/en-us/defender-xdr/streaming-api). |
+| Hide or mask fields | Defender data isn't masked. | Review who can access raw data in Defender. Use [Defender RBAC](transition-unified-rbac), [device groups](/en-us/defender-endpoint/machine-groups), and [Defender for Identity scoped access](/en-us/defender-for-identity/configure-scoped-access). |
+| Filter out known-benign events | You might see more alerts. | Add exclusions to your [custom detection queries](/en-us/defender-xdr/custom-detection-rules), or create an [alert tuning rule](/en-us/defender-xdr/investigate-alerts#tune-an-alert) in Defender. |
+| [Data export rules](/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/logs-data-export) | They stop exporting new data. [Streaming export from Defender](/en-us/defender-xdr/streaming-api) exports the original data, not the transformed data, so the volume and content at the destination can change. | Use streaming export from Defender. |
+| [Summary rules](summary-rules), search jobs, and other jobs that read the table | They stop getting new data, and so do the tables they fill. | Keep the table at 180 days or more. These jobs need the data in the workspace. |
+
+### Check whether you're affected
+
+To check whether a DCR changes an XDR table:
+
+1. In the Defender portal, go to **Setup & configuration** > **Data management** > **Data & connectors**, and select the **Tables** tab. Check the **Transformation Rules** column for the XDR table. It shows **Filter** or **Split** when a [filter or split rule](transformation-filter-split) is active. A split rule also creates a table with an `_SPLT` suffix, for example `DeviceProcessEvents_SPLT`.
+2. Check the table schema for [custom columns that end in `_CF`](/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/tutorial-workspace-transformations-portal).
+3. Check your [data export rules](/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/logs-data-export) and [summary rules](summary-rules) for the table.
+4. If you have more than one workspace, check each one. Each workspace has its own DCR and its own recommendations.
+5. To list workspace DCRs that change XDR tables, run this query in [Azure Resource Graph Explorer](/en-us/azure/governance/resource-graph/first-query-portal). You need Reader access to the subscriptions that hold your workspaces; otherwise the results are incomplete.
+
+```kusto
+resources
+| where type =~ "microsoft.operationalinsights/workspaces"
+| extend DcrId = tolower(tostring(properties.defaultDataCollectionRuleResourceId))
+| where isnotempty(DcrId)
+| project WorkspaceName = name, subscriptionId, DcrId
+| join kind=inner (
+    resources
+    | where type =~ "microsoft.insights/datacollectionrules" and kind =~ "WorkspaceTransforms"
+    | extend DcrId = tolower(id)
+    | mv-expand flow = properties.dataFlows
+    | mv-expand stream = flow.streams
+    | extend TableName = replace_string(tostring(stream), "Microsoft-Table-", ""),
+             Transformation = tostring(flow.transformKql)
+    | where Transformation !~ "source"
+    | project DcrId, DcrName = name, TableName, Transformation
+) on DcrId
+| project WorkspaceName, subscriptionId, DcrName, TableName, Transformation
+```
+
+The query lists only the DCR that's linked to each workspace, and skips DCRs that pass the data through unchanged. Check the results for the tables that appear in your **Lower Defender data costs** recommendations.
+
+### Choose an option for each table
+
+**Option 1: Keep your DCR working**
+
+Keep the table ingested in your Microsoft Sentinel workspace. The DCR stays in place and keeps running.
+
+1. In the Defender portal, go to **Setup & configuration** > **Data management** > **Data & connectors**, and select the **Tables** tab.
+2. Select the table, then select **Manage table**. For details, see [Configure table settings in Microsoft Sentinel](manage-table-tiers-retention).
+3. Set the analytics retention to **180 days or more**, and save.
+
+Do this before you select **Configure workspace**. Data that was already deleted before you change the setting isn't restored.
+
+Additional charges apply when you extend retention beyond the 90 days included with ISOC. For details and pricing, see [Data ingestion, retention, and billing for ISOC in Microsoft Defender](/en-us/defender-xdr/integrated-security-operations-data-billing-retention).
+
+**Option 2: Use the data in Defender**
+
+Keep the table's analytics retention under 180 days. When you select **Configure workspace**, ingestion stops for the table, and you use the original data in Defender, which is kept for 90 days:
+
+- **Added fields (`_CF`):** calculate them in the query. The source data is in the Defender table. See [Update Microsoft Sentinel content to use Advanced Hunting tables](transition-advanced-hunting-tables).
+- **Exports:** use [streaming export from Defender](/en-us/defender-xdr/streaming-api).
+- **Alert noise:** add exclusions to your [custom detection queries](/en-us/defender-xdr/custom-detection-rules), or create an [alert tuning rule](/en-us/defender-xdr/investigate-alerts#tune-an-alert).
+- **Access:** set [device groups](/en-us/defender-endpoint/machine-groups) and [Defender for Identity scope](/en-us/defender-for-identity/configure-scoped-access), and review [imported roles](transition-unified-rbac).
+
+Changes to table retention can take up to 48 hours to appear in SOC optimization.
+
+### UEBA and DeviceLogonEvents
+
+This applies to you if UEBA is turned on and a data collection rule (DCR) changes the **DeviceLogonEvents** table in your Microsoft Sentinel workspace.
+
+UEBA processes the logon data that comes from Defender XDR only when no DCR applies to the DeviceLogonEvents table in your workspace. This keeps the data that UEBA processes in line with your DCR.
+
+- To let UEBA process this data, stop the DCR on the DeviceLogonEvents table. Before you stop it, check what the DCR does. If it hides or masks sensitive fields, review who can access the raw data in Defender.
+- If you keep the DCR, UEBA doesn't process the Defender XDR logon data.
+
+For more information, see [Update UEBA to use Microsoft Defender XDR data](transition-ueba-to-xdr-data).
+
+## Review retention and ingestion
+
+Before making ingestion changes, review the retention available for the Microsoft Defender data that you're transitioning.
+
+Eligible ISOC customers receive 90 days of included retention for supported Microsoft Defender data, Azure Activity data, and Office 365 Activity data.
+
+If you need to keep a DCR working on a table, set that table's retention to 180 days or more before you select **Configure workspace**. See Check data collection rules and transformations.
+
+For information about supported data, retention, and billing, see [Data ingestion, retention, and billing for ISOC in Microsoft Defender](/en-us/defender-xdr/integrated-security-operations-data-billing-retention).
+
+After you complete all **Lower Defender data costs** recommendations, stop ingesting Defender XDR data into Log Analytics for the supported Defender XDR tables in the workspace. In the Defender portal, go to **Setup & configuration** > **Data management** > **Data & connectors**, select the **Tables** tab, and then select **Configure workspace**. Stopping this ingestion lowers your costs.
+
+For more information, see [Optimize Microsoft Defender XDR data ingestion](transition-optimize-xdr-ingestion).
\ No newline at end of file

+# Update UEBA to use Microsoft Defender XDR data | Microsoft Learn
+
+When you transition an existing Microsoft Sentinel deployment, User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA) uses supported Microsoft Defender XDR data directly instead of relying on the same first-party data being ingested into a Microsoft Sentinel workspace.
+
+UEBA outputs continue to be stored in Microsoft Sentinel workspaces. Output from data processed from XDR is sent to the primary workspace. You can select the XDR source tables in the primary workspace's UEBA settings. For data processed from Log Analytics tables, whether ingested through connectors or other means, output is sent to the workspace where UEBA is enabled, which can be a primary or secondary workspace. You can change the Log Analytics source tables selected in UEBA settings.
+
+For customers with a single workspace, the change to Microsoft Defender XDR-backed UEBA is seamless. If you use multiple workspaces or Data Collection Rules (DCRs), review the changes that might affect your existing UEBA configuration before you onboard.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- If you use multiple workspaces, review workspace-specific content that depends on UEBA output.
+- If you have UEBA-enabled Microsoft Sentinel workspaces that aren't connected to the Microsoft Defender portal, connect them before the transition and wait 30 days so that UEBA baselines can be reaccumulated.
+
+The table UEBA supports for this process is `DeviceLogonEvents`. Data from this table transitions seamlessly to the Defender tables, subject to the DCR behavior described in the following sections. The list of supported tables will be updated based on the sources UEBA supports.
+
+## Transition UEBA for a single workspace
+
+### Existing UEBA customers
+
+For existing UEBA deployments with a single Microsoft Sentinel workspace, the change to Microsoft Defender XDR-backed UEBA happens seamlessly if there are no DCRs in place for the originating table.
+
+If your environment has an existing DCR configured for the supported tables, UEBA continues to process the data from Log Analytics. If you stop the DCR on the table, UEBA transitions to the XDR table within 24 hours.
+
+Important
+
+During this window, UEBA still processes events from the XDR table, and DCR filtering doesn't apply to the UEBA output in the workspace. To mitigate this window, you can apply the same DCR to the UEBA tables (`behaviorAnalytics` and `Anomalies`) to avoid data exposure.
+
+Important
+
+If you stop ingestion to the Log Analytics tables, you need to stop the DCRs on those tables for UEBA to transition to the XDR table. This transition takes up to 24 hours.
+
+UEBA output derived from supported Microsoft Defender XDR, Log Analytics, and third-party data continues to be available in the UEBA tables in your Microsoft Sentinel workspace.
+
+Third-party data continues to reach UEBA through Microsoft Sentinel data connectors.
+
+Don't disable and re-enable UEBA as part of the transition. Doing so deletes existing UEBA profiles and baselines. No separate UEBA transition is required.
+
+### Customers without UEBA
+
+If UEBA isn't currently enabled:
+
+1. Complete the required Microsoft Sentinel workspace onboarding.
+2. Open the UEBA settings experience.
+3. Enable UEBA and any required directory synchronization.
+4. In your primary workspace, connect your supported Microsoft Defender XDR data sources to UEBA. You can connect them individually or use the recommended bulk option. In your secondary workspaces, you can connect only Log Analytics tables.
+5. Connect any third-party data sources that you want UEBA to process.
+
+UEBA uses supported Microsoft Defender XDR data as its first-party input. You don't need to separately ingest the same supported first-party data into Microsoft Sentinel for UEBA.
+
+## Transition UEBA for multiple workspaces
+
+UEBA output derived from supported Microsoft Defender XDR data is written to your primary workspace and can only be configured in the primary workspace's UEBA settings. UEBA output derived from third-party and other non-XDR data remains associated with the workspace where the source data is ingested.
+
+There isn't an option to ingest Microsoft Defender XDR-derived UEBA output in a non-primary workspace. However, you can connect Log Analytics tables to UEBA in secondary workspaces, and UEBA reads from the Log Analytics table.
+
+## Review DCR behavior
+
+If you use Data Collection Rules (DCRs) to filter first-party data used by UEBA, the existing filtering doesn't apply when UEBA processes the corresponding Microsoft Defender XDR data directly.
+
+Review the implications of the following configurations:
+
+- When you enable a DCR on an XDR source, UEBA stops processing that source within 24 hours. During this window, you can also apply a DCR to the UEBA table to avoid data exposure.
+- When a DCR is enabled for a supported UEBA table and you stop ingestion to that table as part of ISOC recommendations, UEBA continues to process that table until you stop the DCR. If ingestion stops, UEBA processes a stale table and doesn't generate new outputs or update baselines.
+
+DCR filtering for third-party data continues to work as before.
+
+There isn't a DCR workaround for Microsoft Defender XDR data used directly by UEBA. Review the impact before onboarding. To continue onboarding with the affected data sources, acknowledge the change or turn off UEBA for those data sources.
+
+## Where UEBA output goes
+
+After the transition, UEBA processes supported Microsoft Defender XDR data at the tenant level. Microsoft Defender XDR-derived UEBA output is mapped to the primary Microsoft Sentinel workspace, while other UEBA output remains in the workspace where its source data is ingested.

englishSummary.summary: The guidance explains that existing Microsoft Sentinel deployments can have UEBA process supported Microsoft Defender XDR data directly while continuing to store outputs in Sentinel. It covers workspace and DCR behavior, with DeviceLogonEvents currently supported.
englishSummary.adminImpact: Review UEBA-dependent content and DCRs before onboarding when using multiple workspaces or DCRs. Unconnected UEBA workspaces must be connected to the Defender portal and allowed 30 days to rebuild baselines. Transitions involving DCRs can take up to 24 hours; don't disable and re-enable UEBA because this deletes existing profiles and baselines.

+# Update permissions and roles with Defender RBAC - Microsoft Defender XDR | Microsoft Learn
+
+Before you transition an existing Microsoft Sentinel deployment to Integrated Security Operations Center (ISOC), make sure users who currently access Microsoft Defender data through the Microsoft Sentinel workspace have the corresponding Microsoft Defender workload access.
+
+Use Defender role-based access control (RBAC) in Microsoft Defender XDR to import supported Microsoft Sentinel roles and assignments. Review the roles and assignments before submitting the import, and activate Defender RBAC separately for any required Microsoft Defender workloads that aren't already active.
+
+Important
+
+Microsoft Sentinel workspace access alone doesn't provide access to the corresponding Microsoft Defender workload data. Complete and validate the permission changes before ingestion changes for the affected data.
+
+## Before you begin
+
+Ask your Defender RBAC administrator to perform the migration.
+
+To import roles, the administrator needs:
+
+- At least the Security Administrator role in Microsoft Entra ID, or all Authorization permissions in Microsoft Defender RBAC.
+- Role-management permissions across all required scopes.
+- Access to the primary Microsoft Sentinel workspace and authorization to onboard the workspace to Defender RBAC. Read access to the workspace alone isn't sufficient.
+- Management access to the Microsoft Defender workloads that need to be included.
+
+To activate Defender RBAC for Microsoft Defender workloads that aren't already active, the administrator must have at least the Security Administrator role in Microsoft Entra ID.
+
+To activate a Microsoft Sentinel workspace in Defender RBAC, the administrator must have the Security Administrator role in Microsoft Entra ID and either Subscription Owner permissions or both User Access Administrator and Microsoft Sentinel Contributor permissions on the workspace. However, the source Microsoft Sentinel workspace doesn't need to be activated in Defender RBAC for this import.
+
+The supported Microsoft Defender destination workloads are:
+
+- Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.
+- Microsoft Defender for Office 365.
+- Microsoft Defender for Identity.
+- Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps.
+
+These workloads are added as destinations only when they're eligible, provisioned, and the importing administrator has role-management permissions across all their scopes.
+
+## How role import works
+
+The import creates Defender RBAC roles and user or group assignments from supported Microsoft Sentinel roles.
+
+For qualifying assignments scoped only to the primary Microsoft Sentinel workspace, the import can add eligible Microsoft Defender workloads that the administrator has permission to manage across all required scopes.
+
+Users receive access to Microsoft Defender data through the resulting Defender RBAC assignments when Defender RBAC is active for the corresponding workload.
+
+Importing roles and activating workloads are separate actions:
+
+- Importing roles doesn't activate Defender RBAC for a workload.
+- Activating a workload doesn't import Microsoft Sentinel roles.
+- If a destination Microsoft Defender workload is already active, imported role assignments can take effect immediately without an additional activation step.
+- The source Microsoft Sentinel workspace doesn't need Defender RBAC activated for the import.
+
+Review the roles, permissions, assignments, and scopes before submitting the import, particularly for workloads where Defender RBAC is already active.
+
+## Import Microsoft Sentinel roles
+
+You can import Microsoft Sentinel roles in two ways: through Microsoft Sentinel settings or the Permissions and roles page.
+
+### Import roles from Microsoft Sentinel settings
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Defender portal](https://security.microsoft.com/)
+2. Go to **Setup & Configuration > Settings > Microsoft Sentinel.**
+3. Select **Upgrade to ISOC**.
+
+    ![Screenshot showing the Upgrade to ISOC button.](media/upgrade-to-isoc-button.png)
+4. In **Get your Sentinel workspace ready for ISOC**, expand **3. Import Sentinel roles into Defender RBAC**.
+5. Select **Go to import roles** to open the role import process.
+
+    ![Screenshot showing the Go to import roles option.](media/import-roles-isoc-sentinel.png)
+6. Continue to Complete the role import.
+
+### Import roles from Permissions and roles
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Defender portal](https://security.microsoft.com/)
+2. Go to **Setup & Configuration > Permissions.**
+3. Under **Microsoft Defender XDR**, select **Roles**.
+4. In the **Get ready for ISOC** banner, select the **Start ISOC role import** button.
+
+    ![Screenshot showing the Start ISOC role import button.](media/start-isoc-role-import-permission.png)
+
+    If the banner provides options to import roles and activate workloads, start with the role import. Don't use the separate **Activate workloads** action before reviewing the roles and assignments.
+5. Continue to Complete the role import.
+
+### Complete the role import
+
+In the **Import roles** wizard:
+
+1. Confirm **Microsoft Sentinel** is selected as an import source.
+
+    Microsoft Sentinel uses your primary workspace for the import. For users and groups who rely on Defender data in secondary Microsoft Sentinel workspaces, see Secondary workspaces role definition.
+
+    You can also select other available workloads if you want to import their existing roles. These workloads are additional import sources; selecting them doesn't make them additional destinations for the Microsoft Sentinel role import.
+2. Select **Next**, and review the roles selected for import.
+
+    Eligible Microsoft Sentinel roles are preselected and required. Review:
+
+    - Role details.
+    - Assigned users and groups.
+    - Permissions.
+    - Additional data sources.
+
+    You can deselect optional roles imported from other workloads.
+
+    Before submitting, confirm that the selected roles and assignments provide the intended permissions and scopes, particularly for destination workloads where Defender RBAC is already active.
+3. Complete the review and submit the import.
+4. Review the import result for each role.
+
+    The import can partially succeed, with some roles imported successfully and others failing.
+
+    If any roles fail to import, review the errors and resolve the failures before activating additional workloads or changing ingestion.
+
+    Don't reimport roles that were imported successfully. Importing the same role again can create duplicate roles and assignments.
+
+## Secondary workspaces role definition
+
+The guided role-import flow adds eligible Defender access only for qualifying primary-workspace assignments.
+
+If your secondary Microsoft Sentinel workspaces contain Defender tables, review access for users and groups who rely on that data as part of your role transfer process.
+
+Importing Sentinel roles from secondary workspaces does not, by itself, grant the corresponding Defender access. Some users may therefore need additional permissions to access the data directly in Defender.
+
+Please follow the next steps:
+
+1. Check existing access first. Users who already have the required Defender permissions, through the primary-workspace migration or other assignments, do not need additional grants. Confirm that their existing access covers the data and activities they need.
+2. Add permissions only where needed. Create or reuse a custom Defender RBAC role.
+3. Select these specific permissions rather than all read or manage permissions:
+
+    1. For read-only hunting, select Security data basics (Read).
+    2. For email and collaboration hunting, also select Email & collaboration metadata (Read).
+
+    **Reference:** current Sentinel import mapping. The management permissions below are needed only when those Defender actions are required, not simply to retain read access.
+
+    | Existing Sentinel role | Permissions in the imported role |
+    | --- | --- |
+    | Sentinel Reader | Security data basics (Read) |
+    | Sentinel Responder | Security data basics (Read), Alerts (Manage), Response (Manage) |
+    | Sentinel Contributor | Security data basics (Read), Alerts (Manage), Response (Manage), Detection tuning (Manage) |
+
+    These roles take effect for the assigned users and groups when the corresponding workload uses Defender RBAC. If activation is required, follow the activation guidance and prepare existing users' access before switching permission models.
+4. Scope the assignment.
+
+    On **Assign users and data sources > Add assignment**,
+
+    - Select the affected users/groups and only the required Defender data sources.
+    - Leave **Include future data sources automatically** unchecked. A Defender data source applies the selected permissions to that service, not just the data copied into a particular workspace.
+    - Select the following as needed:
+        - **Microsoft Defender for Endpoint** for device data
+        - **Microsoft Defender for Office 365** for email and collaboration data
+        - **Microsoft Defender for Identity** for identity workload data
+        - **Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps** for cloud-app activity
+    - Apply resource restrictions supported by each service.
+        - For Endpoint, review device-group access separately.
+        - Do not configure Sentinel workspace permissions. Workload-level grants may expose additional tables and do not recreate the original workspace's table restrictions.
+        - Review that additional data access and approve any broader access before assigning the roles.
+5. Validate access and dependent content.
+
+    - Have representative affected users confirm access to the data and history they need.
+    - Check the intended resource restrictions.
+    - Update and test queries, detections, and automation that previously used the workspace copies. Permission changes do not redirect those queries or migrate historical data.
+
+## Activate the required workloads
+
+After the import results are reviewed and any failures are resolved, activate Defender RBAC for the required Microsoft Defender workloads that aren't already active.
+
+If a destination workload is already active, its imported assignments can already be in effect. Review those permissions and scopes before proceeding.
+
+For workloads that aren't active:
+
+1. Review the imported Defender RBAC roles and assignments together with any existing legacy access.
+2. Select **Activate workloads** or **Workload settings** from the **Permissions and roles** page.
+3. Enable Defender RBAC for each required Microsoft Defender workload that isn't already active.
+4. Confirm the activation and review the resulting role assignments and workload scopes.
+
+You don't need to activate Defender RBAC for the source Microsoft Sentinel workspace to complete this import.
+
+## Validate effective access
+
+Before you continue with ingestion changes:
+
+1. Ask affected users to confirm that they can access the required Microsoft Defender data and actions.
+2. Validate the permissions for each required workload.
+3. Validate any resource or workload-specific scopes.
+4. Review users whose Microsoft Sentinel access comes from role assignments at the resource-group or subscription level. Don't assume that inherited access was included in the import. Verify the resulting assignments and configure any missing access as needed.
+5. Confirm that users who previously relied on Microsoft Sentinel workspace permissions have the corresponding Microsoft Defender access they need.
+
+Don't assume that restrictions or scopes configured for Microsoft Sentinel are reproduced automatically in Microsoft Defender.
+
+Note
+
+This process doesn't change data ingestion and doesn't automatically migrate application or automation permissions. Review automation identities and application permissions separately before changing ingestion.
+
+If the role-import option isn't available or role import is disabled, ask your Defender RBAC administrator to verify their permissions and feature availability.
+
+## Further guidance
+

+- [Import roles](/en-us/defender-xdr/import-rbac-roles)
+- [Activate Defender RBAC](/en-us/defender-xdr/activate-defender-rbac)

+# Update workbooks to use Advanced Hunting data - Microsoft Defender XDR | Microsoft Learn
+
+Workbooks can query Microsoft Defender XDR data directly by using Advanced Hunting, without requiring the same data to be ingested into a workspace.
+
+You can update existing workbooks to use Advanced Hunting data or create new workbooks that query Microsoft Defender XDR data directly.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+Before you begin, make sure you have:
+
+- Your tenant is [eligible for ISOC](/en-us/defender-xdr/isoc-overview).
+- To create and edit workbooks, either the **Workbooks** Unified RBAC permission with **Manage** access or the **Security Administrator** role.
+- Access to the scopes and workloads used by the workbook queries.
+
+Workbook permissions don't grant access to the underlying data. Data access and scoping are enforced when the query runs.
+
+For example, a user can open a workbook that contains Defender for Endpoint data, but the workbook tile returns an error if the user doesn't have access to that data.
+
+For more information, see [Update permissions and roles with Unified RBAC](transition-unified-rbac).
+
+## Create a workbook using Advanced Hunting data
+
+The **Workbooks** page includes example workbooks that use Microsoft Defender XDR data.
+
+To create your own workbook:
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Defender portal](https://security.microsoft.com/).
+2. Select **Dashboards & reports** > **Workbooks**.
+3. Select **+ Add workbook**.
+4. Select **Edit**.
+5. In the query section, select **Advanced Hunting** as the data source.
+6. Add or update the query for the workbook tile.
+7. Save the workbook.
+
+## Update an existing workbook
+
+When you stop ingesting a supported Microsoft Defender XDR table into a workspace, update any workbooks that query that table.
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Defender portal](https://security.microsoft.com/).
+2. Select **Dashboards & reports** > **Workbooks** and open the workbook you want to update.
+3. Select **Edit**.
+4. Change the query data source to **Advanced Hunting**.
+5. Review the query and confirm that the table names are available in Advanced Hunting. Most table names remain the same.
+6. Update any table or column references that differ in the Advanced Hunting schema.
+7. Validate the workbook tiles, filters, and parameters.
+
+For information about schema and data-type differences, see [Update Microsoft Sentinel content to use Advanced Hunting tables](transition-advanced-hunting-tables).
+
+## Work with workbooks across workspaces
+
+When one or more workspaces are connected, the **Workbooks** page includes a **Workspace** column that shows where each workbook is saved.
+
+- A workspace name indicates that the workbook is saved to that workspace.
+- **None** indicates that the workbook is saved at the tenant level.
+
+You can filter the workbook list by workspace directly from the **Workbooks** page.
+
+When you save a workbook, choose whether to save it to a specific workspace or at the tenant level.

-# Data ingestion and billing for ISOC in Microsoft Defender - Microsoft Defender XDR | Microsoft Learn
+# Data ingestion, retention, and billing for ISOC in Microsoft Defender - Microsoft Defender XDR | Microsoft Learn
 
 Integrated Security Operations Center (ISOC) in Microsoft Defender supports Microsoft security data and additional Microsoft and non-Microsoft security data.
 
-Note
-
-ISOC is in preview. Capabilities and availability might change during the preview period.
-
 ## How data is handled
 
 Native Microsoft Defender data is available directly in the Microsoft Defender experience and doesn't need to be separately ingested into an ISOC workspace.
 
-Other supported Microsoft and non-Microsoft data can be connected through an ISOC workspace by using data connectors.
+Other supported Microsoft and non-Microsoft data can be connected through an ISOC workspace by using [data connectors](/en-us/azure/sentinel/connect-data-sources?tabs=defender-portal).
 
 ## Microsoft security data
 
@@ -71,22 +67,105 @@ ISOC supports Microsoft security data from the following sources:
 - Microsoft Defender for Identity
 - Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps
 - Microsoft Defender for Cloud
-- Microsoft Entra Identity Protection logs
-- Azure Activity and audit logs through a connector
-- Office 365 Activity and audit logs through a connector
+- Microsoft Entra
 
 Eligible customers with Microsoft Defender Suite, Microsoft 365 E5, or Microsoft 365 E7 can use supported Microsoft Defender security data as part of the ISOC experience.
 
-Note
-
-During this phase of the preview, eligible customers receive 30 days of included retention for Defender data.
-
 For Microsoft 365 E5 plan details and pricing, see [Microsoft 365 E5 for Enterprise](https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/enterprise/e5#Pricing).
 
 To compare the security capabilities included with Microsoft 365 enterprise plans, see [Microsoft 365 Security Enterprise Plans](https://www.microsoft.com/security/pricing/enterprise-plans).
 
+### 90-day retention
+
+Starting November 15, 2026, eligible customers receive up to 90 days of included retention for supported Microsoft Defender data.
+
+The retention benefit applies at the workload level. As additional supported tables become available for an included workload, they'll also be included in the retention benefit.
+
+The following tables and data sources are currently included:
+
+- **Alerts**
+
+    - `AlertEvidence`
+    - `AlertInfo`
+- **Behaviors**
+
+    Retention varies by underlying source; 90-day retention applies only to supported, enabled sources.
+
+    - `BehaviorEntities` (Preview)
+    - `BehaviorInfo` (Preview)
+- **Microsoft Defender for Cloud**
+
+    A full 90-day history is expected by January 3, 2027 for data covered by the current rollout.
+
+    - `CloudPolicyEnforcementEvents`
+    - `CloudKeyVaultEvents` (Preview)
+    - `CloudProcessEvents`
+    - `CloudStorageAggregatedEvents` (Preview)
+    - `CloudAuditEvents`
+    - `CloudDnsEvents`
+- **Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps**
+
+    - `CloudAppEvents`
+    - `OAuthAppInfo` (Preview)
+- **Microsoft Defender for Endpoint**
+
+    - `DeviceEvents`
+    - `DeviceFileCertificateInfo`
+    - `DeviceFileEvents`
+    - `DeviceImageLoadEvents`
+    - `DeviceInfo`
+    - `DeviceLogonEvents`
+    - `DeviceNetworkEvents`
+    - `DeviceNetworkInfo`
+    - `DeviceProcessEvents`
+    - `DeviceRegistryEvents`
+    - `DisruptionAndResponseEvents`
+- **Microsoft Defender for Identity**
+
+    - `IdentityDirectoryEvents`
+    - `IdentityEvents` (Preview)
+    - `IdentityLogonEvents`
+    - `IdentityQueryEvents`
+- **Microsoft Defender for Office 365**
+
+    - `CallActivityEvents`
+    - `CampaignInfo` (Preview)
+    - `EmailAttachmentInfo`
+    - `EmailEvents`
+    - `EmailPostDeliveryEvents`
+    - `EmailUrlInfo`
+    - `FileMaliciousContentInfo` (Preview)
+    - `MessageEvents`
+    - `MessagePostDeliveryEvents`
+    - `MessageUrlInfo`
+    - `UrlClickEvents`
+- **Microsoft Entra**
+
+    - `EntraIdSignInEvents`
+    - `EntraIdSpnSignInEvents`
+    - `GraphAPIAuditEvents`
+
+### Extend Microsoft Defender data retention
+
+You can extend retention for supported Microsoft Defender data up to a maximum of 180 days.
+
+Extended retention applies to new data after you enable it. Data that was collected before you enabled extended retention isn't backfilled.
+
+Additional charges apply when you extend retention beyond the retention included with ISOC.
+
 ## Additional Microsoft and non-Microsoft security data
 
-An ISOC workspace is required to ingest additional Microsoft and non-Microsoft security data through more than 500 data connectors.
+An ISOC workspace is required to ingest additional Microsoft and non-Microsoft security data through [more than 500 data connectors](/en-us/azure/sentinel/data-connectors-reference).
+
+Additional Microsoft and non-Microsoft security data is billed separately from the Microsoft security data included with the ISOC benefit. Ingested data can be retained for up to 90 days as part of the ISOC ingestion experience.
+
+Additional ingestion and retention charges will apply depending on the data you ingest and how long you retain it.
+
+## Choose a retention option
+
+Use the retention option that matches how you plan to use the data:
+
+- Use interactive retention for data that analysts need for investigations, hunting, and ongoing security operations.
+- Use data lake retention for data that you keep primarily for longer-term analysis, audit, or compliance scenarios.
 
-Additional ingestion charges might apply depending on the data you ingest.

+Additional charges apply when you extend retention beyond the retention included with ISOC.

-### How data tiers and retention work
-
-For regional support, see [Data lake retention availability](geographical-availability-data-residency#supported-regions).
-
-You can retain data in Microsoft Sentinel in one of two tiers:
-
-- **Analytics tier**: This tier makes data available for alerting, hunting, workbooks, and all Microsoft Sentinel features. It retains data in two states:
-
-    - **Analytics retention**: In this "hot" state, data is fully available for real-time analytics, including high-performance queries, analytics rules, and threat hunting. By default, Microsoft Sentinel and Microsoft Defender XDR retain data in this tier for 30 days. You can extend the retention period of all tables to up to two years at a prorated monthly long-term retention charge. You can extend the retention period of Microsoft Sentinel solution tables to 90 days for free.
-    - **Total retention**: By default, all data in the analytics tier is mirrored to the data lake for the same retention period. You can extend the retention of your data in the lake beyond the analytics retention, for up to 12 years of total retention at a low cost.
-- **Data Lake tier**: In this low-cost "cold" tier, Microsoft Sentinel retains your data in the data lake only. Data in the Data Lake tier isn't available for real-time analytics features and threat hunting. However, you can access data in the lake whenever you need it through [KQL jobs](datalake/kql-jobs), analyze trends over time by running scheduled KQL or Spark jobs, and aggregate insights from incoming data at a regular cadence by using summary rules.
-- **XDR data**: By default, Microsoft Defender XDR threat hunting data is always available in the Analytics tier for 30 days. You can extend retention of this data in the Analytics tier up to 90 days, which incurs ingestion costs, while storage remains free. Extending retention beyond 90 days in the Analytics tier also incurs storage costs. You can also ingest exclusively into the Data Lake tier, but the data remains available in the Analytics tier for 30 days. Ingesting XDR data directly into the Data Lake tier is more cost-effective, but it involves ingestion, storage, and processing costs. In this option, customers still get 30 days' worth of data in the Analytics tier at no additional cost.
-

-# Configure Table Settings in Microsoft Sentinel | Microsoft Learn
+# Manage tables, tiers, and retention in Sentinel | Microsoft Learn
 
 The Microsoft Defender portal provides a centralized experience for configuring table-level data retention and tier settings across Microsoft Sentinel and Microsoft Defender XDR. You can view and manage retention settings, switch between Analytics and Data Lake tiers, and optimize storage based on operational and cost requirements.
 
-This article explains how to configure retention and tier settings for Microsoft Sentinel and Defender XDR tables in the Microsoft Defender portal. It also explains how to use Table insights, a built-in monitoring feature that surfaces ingestion health data for each table in your workspace.
+For an overview of the **Data & connectors** experience, see [Manage data in Microsoft Sentinel and Defender](manage-data-overview).
 
-For more information about how data tiers and retention work, see [Manage data tiers and retention in Microsoft Sentinel](manage-data-overview).
+Note
+
+If you use Integrated Security Operations Center (ISOC), see [Manage tables, tiers, and retention in ISOC](manage-table-tiers-retention-isoc). Review [Data ingestion and billing for ISOC in Microsoft Defender](/en-us/defender-xdr/integrated-security-operations-data-billing-retention) for eligibility and included retention before changing table settings. The general retention ranges in this article don't establish which settings are supported for an individual ISOC XDR table. The XDR retention thresholds and cost examples describe the existing Microsoft Sentinel XDR ingestion experience, not the ISOC retention benefit.

-## Use Table insights to monitor table health
-
-Table insights is a built-in monitoring view on the Tables page in the Microsoft Defender portal. It gives security and platform engineers a single table-level view of ingestion health across a Microsoft Sentinel workspace, including tables populated by third-party data connectors. Use it to spot silent connector failures, investigate cost spikes, validate a new connector onboarding, and identify tables that might need a different tier or retention setting.
-
-Review the Table insights section and table grid together to understand whether a table is healthy, expensive, or misconfigured.
-
-| Signal | What it shows | How to use it |
-| --- | --- | --- |
-| **Ingestion volume per tier** | The rolling 30-day total of gigabytes ingested into the Analytics and Data Lake tiers for the current workspace | Compare how much data each tier is receiving before you move tables between tiers or shorten retention. |
-| **Table ingestion fluctuations** | Tables whose last 24-hour ingestion volume differs from the same day last week by at least the configured fluctuation threshold | Investigate large drops or spikes first. A negative value can indicate an upstream collection issue, while a positive value can signal unexpected cost growth. |
-| **Top 5 tables by daily ingestion volume** | The tables that drove the most daily ingestion during the last 30 days | Use this view to identify the main cost drivers in the workspace and decide whether a transformation or tier change might help. |
-| **Last data received** | How long it has been since the table last received a record | Use this value to detect a connector that has gone silent, especially after a deployment or credential change. |
-| **Avg. daily ingestion** | The average number of gigabytes per day over the lookback window | Compare this value with retention settings to find tables that are storing more data than you need for active investigations. |
-| **Est. daily ingestion cost** | The estimated daily ingestion cost for the table's current tier | Use this estimate to prioritize which tables to optimize first when costs increase. |
-| **Volume anomaly** | The signed percentage change from the baseline ingestion pattern | Focus on large positive values for unexpected cost growth and large negative values for possible data collection failures. |
-
-To view all table insights and investigate table behavior:
-
-1. Sign in to the Microsoft Defender portal.
-2. Go to **Microsoft Sentinel** > **Configuration** > **Tables**.
-3. Select **View all**.
-
-    [![Screenshot that shows where the View all button is located in the Table insights section of the page.](media/manage-table-tiers-retention/view-all-table-insights.png)](media/manage-table-tiers-retention/view-all-table-insights.png#lightbox)
-4. Review all insights.
-5. (Optional) Add additional filters such as:
-
-    - Minimum fluctuation percentage.
-    - Minimum fluctuation volume by kilobytes (KB), megabytes (MB), or gigabytes (GB).
-6. (Optional) Sort the table by selecting one of the headers.
-
-Table insights is useful in scenarios such as:
-
-- If a third-party connector silently stops sending data, sort by **Last data received** and review the **Table ingestion fluctuations** card for tables that dropped to zero ingestion in the last 24 hours compared to the same period last week.
-- If a noisy connector causes an unexpected cost spike, review **Top 5 tables by daily ingestion volume**, then inspect **Volume anomaly** and **Est. daily ingestion cost** to find the table that needs transformation or tier review.
-- If you just onboarded a new third-party data connector, confirm that its destination table appears in the grid, is receiving data, and is on the expected tier.
-- If you need to right-size table settings, compare **Avg. daily ingestion**, **Est. daily ingestion cost**, **Tier**, and **Retention** to identify candidates for the Data Lake tier or shorter retention.
-- If detections suddenly drop, review the fluctuations card for tables that show a 100 percent decrease and correlate those tables with the detections that stopped firing.
-
-### Table insights limitations
-
-Keep the following limits in mind when you interpret the **Table insights** data:
-
-| Area | Limitation |
-| --- | --- |
-| Lookback window | Ingestion volume cards show only the last 30 days. Fluctuations compare the last 24 hours with the same day of the previous week, so they don't account for longer seasonal patterns such as month-end batch jobs. |
-| Fluctuation thresholds | By default, fluctuations require at least a 10 percent change and 1 megabyte of absolute change. Tables below 1 MB per day aren't evaluated and won't appear on the card even if they fully stop sending data. |
-| Cost estimates | The **Est. daily ingestion cost** value is based on public list price for the table's current tier and region. It doesn't reflect commitment-tier discounts, reservations, or private pricing. |
-| Tier coverage | Auxiliary, Basic Logs, and Data Lake tier tables are listed, but the **Volume anomaly** signal is currently optimized for Analytics tier tables. Results for Data Lake tier tables can be less precise. |
-| Alerting | **Table insights** is a visualization surface only. To alert on table health, such as when a connector goes silent, create a scheduled analytics rule that uses the `SentinelHealth` table or a Kusto Query Language (KQL) query against `Usage` or a table-specific schema. |
-| Multi-workspace view | **Table insights** shows data for the currently selected workspace only. If you manage multiple workspaces, switch workspaces to review each one separately. |

+## Lower Defender data costs recommendations
+
+SOC optimization shows a **Lower Defender data costs** recommendation when a Microsoft Defender XDR table is ingested into a Microsoft Sentinel workspace, and the same data is available in Microsoft Defender for 90 days as part of ISOC. For more information, see [Data ingestion, retention, and billing for ISOC](/en-us/defender-xdr/integrated-security-operations-data-billing-retention).
+
+Each recommendation covers one table in one workspace. The recommendation shows the analytics rules, workbooks, and playbooks that use the table.
+
+Completing a recommendation doesn't lower costs by itself. Costs go down only after you stop ingestion for the supported Defender XDR tables with **Configure workspace**.
+
+Important
+
+You can't stop ingestion for a single table. **Configure workspace** stops ingesting data into Log Analytics for the supported Defender XDR tables in the workspace at the same time, except tables with analytics retention set to 180 days or more, which stay ingested. messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Defender: Similar cases comes to the unified security operations platform
messageCenterItems.summary: A new Similar cases tab in the Microsoft Defender portal lists up to 20 related incidents by alert titles or entities, aiding analysts in identifying patterns. The Associated incidents card is renamed Recommended correlations. Public preview is available now; full rollout completes by early December 2026. No action required.
messageCenterItems.body:
What and why

A new Similar cases tab appears on the incident page in the Microsoft Defender portal. The tab lists up to 20 incidents that share alert titles or entities with the current incident, helping security analysts identify recurring patterns and see how similar cases were handled. The Similarity reason column shows why each incident appears in the list.

This update brings the Similar incidents experience from Microsoft Sentinel in the Azure portal to the unified security operations platform. As part of this update, the Associated incidents card on the Summary tab will be renamed Recommended correlations. Similar cases show separate cases that share alert titles or entities, while Recommended correlations identifies cases that are likely part of the same attack. The content of the renamed card will not change.

Rollout schedule

  • Public Preview: Available now.
  • General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin and complete rollout in early December 2026.

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Security analysts who investigate cases in the Microsoft Defender portal, including Microsoft Sentinel customers who use the Defender portal

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Defender portal
  • Microsoft Defender XDR
  • Microsoft Sentinel in the Defender portal

What will happen

  • A new Similar cases tab will appear on the case page: 

  • The tab will list up to 20 cases that share alert titles or entities with the current incident.
  • The Similarity reason column will show why an incident appears in the list. Analysts can hover over the info icon to view the items the cases have in common: 

  • The Associated incidents card on the incident Summary tab will be renamed Recommended correlations.
  • The content of the renamed card will not change.

Action required and recommendations

No action is required to prepare for this change.

Learn more

  • Alert correlation and incident merging in the Microsoft Defender portal - Microsoft Defender XDR | Microsoft Learn
  • Investigate incident cases in the Microsoft Defender portal - Microsoft Defender XDR | Microsoft Learn
  • Investigate incidents in the Microsoft Defender portal (Legacy) - Microsoft Defender XDR | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.
